scope: Last-resort umbrella subfield for agricultural and biological sciences research that spans multiple subfields of this field or does not fit cleanly into any single one of them, e.g. broad agricultural economics, rural development, general agri-food systems work, or general biology not tied to a specific subdiscipline. Only use when a topic clearly belongs to this field but not to any of its named subfields; per ASJC convention this is a last-resort bucket, not a preferred home. ARBITRATION vs Economics and Econometrics [Economics, Econometrics and Finance] and Development [Social Sciences]: agricultural economics and policy is named as belonging to Economics and Econometrics (2002); rural development and rural-sociology framing is named as belonging to Development (3303); this card keeps only genuinely cross-cutting or unclassified agricultural/biological-science topics, as a true last resort.
includes: agricultural science topics that combine multiple named agricultural subfields (e.g. agronomy, animal science, soil science) with no single specific home; general biology or agricultural-science research not tied to a specific subdiscipline, pending clearer classification; general/multidisciplinary agri-food systems; agricultural extension and innovation diffusion; general biotechnology applied to agriculture; cross-cutting agricultural sustainability
excludes: agri-environmental policy, governance, and monitoring frameworks (sustainability-assessment/policy framing rather than agricultural-science framing) -> Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law ; agricultural education and extension pedagogy (teaching/training framing rather than agricultural-science framing) -> Education ; agricultural economics, farm-level economic analysis, and agricultural policy studied as economics -> Economics and Econometrics ; rural development, rural sociology, and developing-region agricultural/social change studied as development studies -> Development
flagship_journals: Agricultural Systems; Agriculture and Human Values; Outlook on Agriculture

scope: Study of crop plants and agricultural production systems: crop breeding and genetics for yield and quality, crop physiology and management, cropping systems and farming practices, and field-crop pest/disease management as applied to production agriculture.
includes: crop breeding and cultivar development; cropping systems and rotations; crop physiology and yield; agronomic management (irrigation, fertilization scheduling); precision agriculture and field-crop technology; seed science; sustainable/conservation farming systems
excludes: general plant biology not tied to crop production -> Plant Science ; soil chemistry, fertility, and pedology as a discipline -> Soil Science ; livestock and animal production -> Animal Science and Zoology
flagship_journals: Agronomy Journal; Field Crops Research; Crop Science; European Journal of Agronomy

scope: Study of animals spanning livestock production science (breeding, nutrition, physiology, husbandry, welfare) and zoology broadly (comparative anatomy, physiology, and biology of domesticated and wild vertebrates), with a production/organismal-biology orientation. NOTE ON VETERINARY: the Veterinary field contains only Equine and Small Animals - there is no general veterinary subfield. Livestock, poultry and farmed-fish health topics belong here, not in Veterinary.
includes: livestock breeding and genetics; animal nutrition and feeding; animal husbandry and welfare; meat and animal product quality; comparative anatomy and physiology; wildlife biology (organismal, non-ecological); reproductive biology of animals; disease, health, biosecurity and infectious pathology of livestock, poultry and farmed animals as a production concern; laboratory-animal science: husbandry, welfare, refinement and models
excludes: ecological/behavioral studies of wild animal populations and communities -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; insects and other arthropods -> Insect Science ; aquatic organisms and fisheries biology -> Aquatic Science
flagship_journals: Journal of Animal Science; Animal; Livestock Science

scope: Study of organisms and ecosystems in marine and freshwater environments, including aquatic biology, limnology, marine biology, fisheries science, and aquaculture, covering both wild aquatic populations and farmed aquatic production.
includes: marine and freshwater biology; limnology; fisheries science and management; aquaculture and mariculture; aquatic invertebrate and vertebrate biology; aquatic ecosystem ecology; aquatic biodiversity and taxonomy
excludes: terrestrial ecology and evolutionary biology -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; physical/chemical oceanography of water bodies -> Oceanography ; processing and quality of harvested seafood products -> Food Science
flagship_journals: Journal of Fish Biology; Aquaculture; Limnology and Oceanography; Aquatic Sciences

scope: Study of relationships between organisms and their environments, evolutionary processes and phylogenetics, animal and plant behavior, and taxonomic/systematic classification of organisms across all kingdoms, spanning population, community, and ecosystem ecology plus macroevolutionary and behavioral biology. ARBITRATION vs Ecology [Environmental Science]: the study OBJECT decides. Organisms, taxa, populations and their evolution, behaviour, life history and classification belong here; the environment or ecosystem studied as a system belongs to Ecology [Environmental Science]. Evolution, phylogenetics, systematics and taxonomy are never Environmental Science. ARBITRATION vs Anthropology [Social Sciences] and Language and Linguistics [Arts and Humanities]: human cultural, social, and linguistic evolution belongs to Anthropology (3314) and Language and Linguistics (1203) respectively; this card keeps the biological evolution, phylogenetics, and behavior of organisms (including the biological basis of human evolution).
includes: community and population ecology; evolutionary biology and phylogenetics; animal behavior and ethology; taxonomy and systematics of any taxon; biodiversity and biogeography; speciation and adaptation; conservation biology (ecological aspects)
excludes: crop- and horticultural-plant-specific physiology, breeding, and agronomy -> Plant Science ; gene-level molecular mechanisms of heredity -> Genetics ; insect-specific applied pest control and economic entomology -> Insect Science ; ecosystem processes, ecosystem services, environmental drivers and stressors, water-body and catchment ecology, or landscape-scale environmental monitoring, where the environment rather than the organism is the object of study -> Ecology ; human cultural and social evolution, and the history of human societies' customs, institutions, and social organization, as opposed to the biological evolution of organisms -> Anthropology ; the evolution, structure, and diversity of human language as a communicative/cultural system, as opposed to the biological evolution of species -> Language and Linguistics
flagship_journals: Ecology; Evolution; Journal of Animal Ecology; Systematic Biology

scope: Study of the composition, processing, preservation, safety, quality, and sensory/nutritional properties of food, including food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering/technology, and consumer/cultural food studies.
includes: food processing and preservation technology; food safety and quality control; food chemistry and biochemistry; food microbiology; sensory science and consumer food studies; nutritional composition of food products; food packaging and storage
excludes: crop and plant biology upstream of harvest -> Plant Science ; clinical human nutrition and dietetics -> Nutrition and Dietetics ; field-level agricultural production practices -> Agronomy and Crop Science ; food as a cultural, social or political object - food culture and identity, food-system governance, food security policy, globalisation of diets -> Geography, Planning and Development
flagship_journals: Journal of Food Science; Food Chemistry; Food Research International; LWT - Food Science and Technology

scope: Study of forest ecosystems and their management: silviculture, forest ecology and dynamics, forest products, agroforestry, and the sustainable management, conservation, and monitoring of woodlands and tree plantations.
includes: silviculture and forest management; forest ecology and dynamics; agroforestry systems; timber and forest products science; forest conservation and restoration; tree physiology and growth; forest inventory and remote sensing of forests
excludes: general plant physiology unrelated to trees or forest stands -> Plant Science ; broader ecosystem/community ecology not forest-specific -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics
flagship_journals: Forest Ecology and Management; Forestry; Canadian Journal of Forest Research; Agroforestry Systems

scope: Study of the cultivation, physiology, breeding, and production of garden and orchard plants: fruits, vegetables, ornamentals, and nursery crops, including horticultural science, landscape horticulture, and postharvest management.
includes: fruit and vegetable production science; ornamental plant cultivation; nursery and greenhouse production; postharvest physiology and handling; landscape and urban horticulture; horticultural breeding and propagation; viticulture and orchard management
excludes: broad-acre field crop agronomy (grains, oilseeds) -> Agronomy and Crop Science ; general plant molecular/physiological biology not tied to cultivated horticultural crops -> Plant Science
flagship_journals: Scientia Horticulturae; HortScience; Postharvest Biology and Technology

scope: Study of insects and related arthropods: their biology, physiology, behavior, ecology, and taxonomy, together with their roles as pests, pollinators, or disease vectors, and applied entomology and pest control.
includes: insect biology and physiology; faunistic and descriptive taxonomic revision of insect groups; insect-plant interactions; insect behavior and pheromone research; integrated pest management; insect pathology and biocontrol agents; pollinator biology
excludes: broader vertebrate animal biology and zoology -> Animal Science and Zoology ; general community/population ecology and evolutionary biology not insect-specific -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; insect studies whose contribution is phylogenetic or evolutionary - molecular phylogenetics, DNA barcoding, cryptic-species delimitation, biodiversity inventory, biogeography - where the discipline is systematics and the taxon is incidental -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics
flagship_journals: Journal of Insect Science; Insect Science; Annual Review of Entomology; Journal of Economic Entomology

scope: Study of plant biology, physiology, genetics, molecular biology, growth, development, stress responses, and interactions with pathogens and the environment, spanning basic and applied botanical research not specific to a named crop- or horticultural-production context. ARBITRATION: mechanism, physiology, molecular biology and stress responses stay here even when studied in a crop species; production framing (yield, management, breeding for performance) goes to Agronomy and Crop Science; anything after harvest goes to Food Science.
includes: plant physiology and development; plant molecular biology and genomics; plant stress and pathogen responses; plant nutrient uptake and metabolism; photosynthesis and plant biochemistry; plant-microbe interactions; plant biotechnology
excludes: herbal/traditional medicinal use of plants -> Complementary and alternative medicine ; post-harvest food processing and quality of plant-derived foods -> Food Science ; gene-level heredity and molecular genetics mechanisms not plant-specific -> Molecular Biology ; plant taxonomy, phylogenetics, and community/population ecology -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics
flagship_journals: Plant Cell; Plant Physiology; New Phytologist; Journal of Experimental Botany

scope: Study of soil formation, composition, chemistry, biology, and physical properties, and their management for agricultural and land-use purposes, including soil fertility, pedology, and soil-plant nutrient relationships.
includes: pedology and soil classification; soil chemistry and fertility; soil microbiology and biology; soil physics and hydrology; soil erosion and conservation; soil-plant nutrient cycling; land management and soil quality assessment
excludes: crop management practices beyond the soil-nutrient relationship -> Agronomy and Crop Science
flagship_journals: Soil Biology and Biochemistry; European Journal of Soil Science; Geoderma; Plant and Soil

scope: Last-resort bucket for humanities and arts research that is genuinely interdisciplinary or does not fit cleanly into one of the other Arts and Humanities subfields (History, Philosophy, Literature, Music, Visual and Performing Arts, Archeology, Classics, Language and Linguistics, Museology, Religious studies). Covers broad humanities scholarship, cultural studies, and cross-cutting humanities theory or method.
includes: interdisciplinary humanities scholarship; cross-cutting humanities theory and method; mythology and folklore studies; general arts scholarship and criticism; humanities pedagogy and curriculum; area/regional studies with a humanities lens; digital humanities methods
excludes: critical/theoretical analysis of culture, identity, ideology and representation -> Cultural Studies ; interdisciplinary social research whose object is society, institutions or policy rather than humanistic interpretation -> General Social Sciences ; religion, theology and religious traditions as the object -> Religious studies

scope: The study and narration of past human events, societies, and change over time through documentary and archival evidence. Covers political, social, cultural, intellectual, and institutional history across periods and regions, including the history of specific domains (medicine, education, religion) when the framing is historical rather than disciplinary.
includes: political and social history; cultural and intellectual history; history of institutions and religion; regional and national historiography; history of specific domains (medicine, education) told as history; early modern and modern historical studies
excludes: history of scientific ideas, methods, and institutions specifically, and philosophy of science -> History and Philosophy of Science ; ancient Greco-Roman history and classical civilization specifically -> Classics ; archaeological excavation and material-culture methods as the primary focus -> Archeology ; collective memory, testimony and memory politics analysed through cultural theory rather than historiography -> Cultural Studies
flagship_journals: American Historical Review; Journal of Modern History; Past & Present

scope: The scientific and humanistic study of human language: its structure, meaning, use, acquisition, history, and evolution. Covers theoretical, descriptive, applied, and historical approaches to language across all levels of analysis. ARBITRATION vs Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics [Agricultural and Biological Sciences]: this card owns the evolution, structure, and diversity of human language as a communicative/cultural system; the biological evolution of non-human communication and behavior belongs to Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics (1105).
includes: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics; historical and comparative linguistics; sociolinguistics and language variation; psycholinguistics and language acquisition; computational and corpus linguistics; philology and classical language studies; language typology and evolution; translation and discourse studies
excludes: literary criticism and analysis of literary works -> Literature and Literary Theory ; pedagogy and classroom language teaching methods -> Education ; the biological evolution of non-human animal communication and behavior, studied as evolutionary biology rather than human language structure/use -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics
flagship_journals: Language; Journal of Linguistics; Linguistic Inquiry; Applied Linguistics; Journal of Pragmatics

scope: Study of past human societies and cultures through material remains: excavation, artifacts, sites, and monuments, spanning prehistoric to historic-period archaeology, archaeological method and science, and landscape/archaeoastronomy studies. ARBITRATION vs Archeology [Social Sciences] (3302): humanistic, art-historical, classical/philological, and heritage-as-culture interpretation of the past stays here; anthropological-method, settlement/society-focused, and archaeometric/scientific archaeology goes to the Social Sciences twin.
includes: excavation and field archaeology; artifact and material culture analysis; prehistoric and historic-period archaeology; interpretation of dated material culture within historical and art-historical frameworks; landscape and settlement archaeology; archaeoastronomy; underwater/maritime archaeology
excludes: documentary/textual history without a material-remains focus -> History ; classical philology and literature of ancient Greece and Rome -> Classics ; settlement-pattern, social-organization, subsistence/technology, and anthropological-method archaeology, including archaeometric and quantitative/scientific analysis, where a social-scientific rather than humanistic/historical framing is primary -> Archeology
flagship_journals: Journal of Archaeological Science; American Journal of Archaeology; Antiquity; World Archaeology

scope: The study of the languages, literature, history, and culture of ancient Greece and Rome, and closely related ancient Mediterranean civilizations. Covers classical philology, ancient history, classical literature and reception, and the broader medieval/Byzantine and Renaissance traditions that carry classical influence forward.
includes: ancient Greek and Latin literature and philology; Greco-Roman history and civilization; classical reception and tradition; Byzantine studies; medieval and early-modern continuations of classical culture; classical archaeology and material culture (textual/cultural framing)
excludes: archaeological excavation, artifact analysis, and material-culture methods as the primary focus -> Archeology ; general literary theory and literature not tied to the classical/ancient world -> Literature and Literary Theory ; general historical scholarship not centered on antiquity or its classical reception -> History
flagship_journals: Classical Quarterly; American Journal of Philology; Journal of Roman Studies; Greece & Rome

scope: Study and practice of preserving, conserving, and restoring cultural heritage: artworks, artifacts, monuments, and historic sites, including conservation science, heritage-materials analysis, and preventive conservation in museums and heritage institutions. This is heritage/cultural conservation, distinct from nature/biodiversity conservation.
includes: conservation and restoration of artworks and artifacts; heritage materials science and analysis; preventive conservation in museums; conservation of historic buildings and monuments; conservation ethics and theory; digital documentation for heritage conservation
excludes: biodiversity and nature/wildlife conservation biology -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; general museum curatorial and collections-management practice -> Museology
flagship_journals: Studies in Conservation; Journal of the American Institute for Conservation; Heritage Science

scope: Study of the historical development of scientific ideas, institutions, and practices, and the philosophical examination of scientific method, knowledge, and reasoning, including the history of specific scientific disciplines and the intellectual/biographical history of scientists.
includes: history of specific sciences (physics, medicine, biology, etc.); philosophy of science and scientific method; history of scientific institutions and practice; biographical/intellectual history of scientists; epistemology of scientific knowledge; historical science-and-society studies
excludes: general philosophy not focused on science -> Philosophy ; teaching/pedagogy of a discipline (e.g. history of mathematics education framed as instructional practice) -> Education
flagship_journals: Isis; British Journal for the Philosophy of Science; Studies in History and Philosophy of Science

scope: The study, interpretation, and theorization of literary texts across languages and periods. Covers literary criticism and theory, national and comparative literatures, literary history, and discourse/narrative analysis applied to literary or cultural texts.
includes: literary criticism and theory; national and comparative literature; literary history and periodization; narrative and discourse analysis of texts; postcolonial and cultural literary studies; literature in media and adaptation studies (film, digital, transmedia)
excludes: ancient Greco-Roman literature and philology specifically -> Classics ; general linguistics not focused on literary texts -> Language and Linguistics ; literacy pedagogy, reading/writing instruction and language-of-instruction policy -> Education
flagship_journals: PMLA; Comparative Literature; New Literary History

scope: The theory and practice of museums, cultural heritage, and collections. Covers museum studies and curation, cultural heritage preservation and interpretation, exhibition design, and the broader study of material and visual culture as it relates to collecting and public display.
includes: museum studies and curation; cultural heritage preservation and interpretation; exhibition design and practice; collections management; material and visual culture studies tied to display/heritage; display, conservation and interpretation of craft and design heritage in collections
excludes: archaeological excavation and artifact analysis as the primary focus (as opposed to museum display/heritage interpretation) -> Archeology ; conservation science/technique for heritage objects as a technical discipline -> Conservation
flagship_journals: Museum Management and Curatorship; Museum International; Journal of Museum Education

scope: The study, history, theory, and practice of music, including musicology, composition, performance, and the cultural and educational dimensions of musical life.
includes: music theory and analysis; music history and historiography; ethnomusicology; composition and performance studies; music psychology and cognition; music education; organology and instrument studies
excludes: film/screen soundtrack and multimedia performance studies -> Visual Arts and Performing Arts
flagship_journals: Journal of the American Musicological Society; Music Theory Spectrum; Ethnomusicology; Journal of Music Theory

scope: The systematic study of fundamental questions about knowledge, existence, value, and reason. Covers ethics, epistemology, metaphysics, logic, and the major historical and contemporary traditions of philosophical thought, including rhetoric and argumentation when framed philosophically.
includes: ethics and moral philosophy; epistemology and metaphysics; logic and argumentation; history of philosophy and philosophical traditions; philosophy of mind and language; rhetoric and philosophical discourse analysis
excludes: philosophy specifically of scientific method, knowledge, and practice, and the history of science -> History and Philosophy of Science
flagship_journals: Mind; Journal of Philosophy; Philosophical Review; Ethics

scope: The academic, comparative, and historical study of religions, religious traditions, beliefs, institutions, and practices, including theology as an object of scholarly study rather than devotional practice. Covers world religions, new and emerging religious movements, and the history and sociology of religion.
includes: comparative religion; theology and religious philosophy; history of religions and denominations; sociology and anthropology of religion; religious movements and revivalism; sacred texts and scripture studies; religious ethics
excludes: religion, ritual, or belief analyzed primarily as a cultural-identity, popular-culture, or media-representation phenomenon rather than as an object of comparative-religion, theological, or historical-religious scholarship -> Cultural Studies ; ethnographic fieldwork on a society's total kinship, ritual, and social organization, where religious practice is one component of a broader anthropological account rather than the primary object of study -> Anthropology ; documentary/political history of religious institutions, denominations, or events studied as historical narrative rather than as comparative or theological religious studies -> History
flagship_journals: Journal of Religion; Religious Studies; Journal for the Scientific Study of Religion; Numen

scope: The study, history, theory, and practice of visual arts (painting, sculpture, photography, film, design) and performing arts (theatre, dance, performance), including art criticism, aesthetics, and visual/material culture.
includes: art history and theory; film and cinema studies; theatre and drama studies; dance studies; visual and material culture studies; aesthetics and art criticism; art education; curatorial and museum studies
excludes: music composition, theory, and musicology -> Music
flagship_journals: Art Bulletin; October; Theatre Journal; Dance Research Journal

scope: The biology of aging and senescence at molecular, cellular, and organismal levels, including the mechanisms that drive age-related decline and the pathways that modulate lifespan and healthspan.
includes: cellular senescence; telomere biology; longevity and lifespan-extension pathways (sirtuins, mTOR, IGF-1); geroscience and biomarkers of aging; oxidative stress and aging; model-organism aging studies (yeast, worm, fly, mouse); age-related molecular and epigenetic changes
excludes: clinical geriatric care and patient management -> Geriatrics and Gerontology
flagship_journals: Aging Cell; Aging (Albany NY); GeroScience; Mechanisms of Ageing and Development

scope: The chemistry of biological molecules and processes: enzyme mechanisms, metabolic pathways, and the structure and reactivity of proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids, studied primarily at the chemical/biophysical level rather than through gene regulation. ARBITRATION vs Biochemistry [Medicine]: fundamental, mechanism-first chemistry of biomolecules (enzyme kinetics, metabolic pathway chemistry, bioenergetics) studied for its own biochemical interest stays here; biochemistry framed around a human disease mechanism, disease biomarker, or clinical/biomedical outcome belongs to Biochemistry [Medicine].
includes: enzyme kinetics and catalytic mechanisms; metabolic pathways and metabolomics; protein biochemistry and structure; lipid, carbohydrate, and nucleic acid chemistry; bioenergetics; biochemical analytical and assay methods
excludes: gene expression and transcriptional/translational regulation mechanisms -> Molecular Biology ; diagnostic and disease-marker biochemistry in a clinical/lab-medicine context -> Clinical Biochemistry ; biochemistry framed around a human disease MECHANISM or clinical outcome (laboratory diagnostics and assay-based disease markers go to Clinical Biochemistry instead) -> Biochemistry
flagship_journals: Journal of Biological Chemistry; Biochemistry; Biochemical Journal; FEBS Journal

scope: The application of physical principles, methods, and instrumentation to biological molecules and systems, including structural biology, biomolecular dynamics, and quantitative biophysical measurement.
includes: structural biology (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, NMR); molecular dynamics and computational biophysics; membrane and single-molecule biophysics; bioenergetics and biophysical chemistry; biomechanics at the molecular/cellular scale; spectroscopic and imaging biophysical methods
excludes: clinical medical imaging devices and instrumentation -> Biomedical Engineering
flagship_journals: Biophysical Journal; Journal of Molecular Biology; Nature Structural & Molecular Biology; Biophysical Reviews

scope: The applied use of biological systems, organisms, or their components to develop products, processes, and industrial technologies, spanning fermentation, bioprocessing, enzyme engineering, and applied microbial/agricultural biotechnology.
includes: industrial fermentation and bioprocessing; enzyme engineering and industrial applications; biotechnological process and product engineering (including with microbial hosts) where the engineered product or process design, not the microbe's own biology or cultivation, is the contribution; natural product discovery and bioprospecting where the engineered production process or product is the contribution; recombinant protein and antibody production; agricultural and food biotechnology
excludes: basic mechanistic gene-function research without an applied/product goal -> Molecular Biology ; medical devices and biomaterials for clinical use -> Biomedical Engineering ; work in which an assay, purification or culture protocol is merely the method - an applied product, process or industrial goal is what makes a topic Biotechnology -> Biochemistry ; bioprospecting and natural-product work where the producing organism is a microorganism and the contribution is the microbial process or its cultivation -> Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology
flagship_journals: Biotechnology and Bioengineering; Trends in Biotechnology; Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology; Journal of Biotechnology

scope: The biology of cancer: oncogenesis, tumor biology, cancer genomics, metastasis, and the molecular and cellular mechanisms specific to malignant transformation and tumor progression, spanning basic and translational research.
includes: oncogenes and tumor-suppressor pathways; tumor microenvironment and metastasis; cancer genomics and mutational landscapes; cancer cell signaling and carcinogenesis; cancer biomarkers; basic tumor immunology
excludes: gene-regulation mechanisms not specific to cancer -> Molecular Biology ; clinical oncology treatment, trials, and patient management -> Oncology
flagship_journals: Cancer Research; Nature Reviews Cancer; Cancer Cell; Oncogene

scope: The structure, organization, and function of cells and their organelles, including intracellular processes such as signaling, division, transport, and adhesion studied at the whole-cell level. ARBITRATION vs Genetics [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: general, cross-cutting whole-cell and whole-organism biology of a research model system belongs here; the same model system studied through a genetic-screen or genomics-centred lens belongs to Genetics. ARBITRATION vs Developmental Biology [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: embryogenesis, morphogenesis, and organogenesis studied for their own sake belong to Developmental Biology (1309); this card keeps general cell-level structure/function and cross-cutting model-organism biology.
includes: organelle structure and function; cytoskeleton and cell motility; cell signaling pathways; cell cycle and division; membrane trafficking and vesicular transport; cell adhesion and junctions; stem cell biology; cellular stress responses; general whole-cell and whole-organism biology of research model systems, studied broadly rather than through any single downstream application
excludes: DNA/RNA-level mechanisms of transcription, replication, and gene regulation -> Molecular Biology ; embryogenesis, morphogenesis, organogenesis and other developmental-biology processes studied for their own sake -> Developmental Biology
flagship_journals: Journal of Cell Biology; Cell; Nature Cell Biology; Molecular Biology of the Cell

scope: The biochemical basis of disease as applied in clinical diagnostics: laboratory analysis of blood and body-fluid biomarkers, clinical enzymology, and biochemical methods used in laboratory medicine.
includes: clinical biomarkers and diagnostic assays; clinical enzymology; laboratory medicine and biochemical testing methods; reference intervals and analytical validation; point-of-care biochemical testing; biochemical disease-marker discovery
excludes: basic, non-clinical enzyme and metabolic chemistry -> Biochemistry
flagship_journals: Clinical Chemistry; Clinical Biochemistry; Annals of Clinical Biochemistry; Clinica Chimica Acta

scope: The biological processes by which organisms grow and develop from fertilization to maturity, including embryogenesis, morphogenesis, cell-fate determination, and organogenesis. ARBITRATION vs Cell Biology [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: this card owns embryogenesis, morphogenesis, and organogenesis; general whole-cell/whole-organism biology of a model system where development is not the specific focus belongs to Cell Biology (1307).
includes: embryogenesis; morphogenesis and pattern formation; cell-fate determination and differentiation; organogenesis; developmental signaling pathways; regeneration biology; evolutionary developmental biology (evo-devo)
excludes: adult stem-cell biology and regenerative medicine applications outside a developmental context -> Cell Biology ; gene-regulatory mechanism studies without a developmental focus -> Molecular Biology ; biology of a research model system where development is not the specific focus (general whole-cell/whole-organism or genetic/genomic framing) -> Cell Biology
flagship_journals: Development; Developmental Biology; Developmental Cell; Genes & Development

scope: The biology of hormones and endocrine glands: hormone synthesis, secretion, and signaling, and the endocrine regulation of metabolism, growth, and physiology, including molecular mechanisms of hormone action.
includes: hormone signaling and receptor biology; endocrine gland physiology; metabolic hormone regulation (insulin, thyroid, steroid hormones); neuroendocrinology; reproductive endocrinology; endocrine disruptors
excludes: clinical management of endocrine disease (diabetes, thyroid disorders) -> Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism ; general (non-hormonal) metabolic biochemistry -> Biochemistry ; clinical diabetes, obesity, thyroid and metabolic disease management -> Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism ; neuroendocrine and autonomic control of physiological state and behaviour -> Endocrine and Autonomic Systems
flagship_journals: Endocrinology; Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism; Molecular and Cellular Endocrinology; Trends in Endocrinology & Metabolism

scope: The study of heredity, gene function, and genetic variation, including classical and population genetics, genomics, genetic epidemiology, and applied genetics in humans, animals, and plants. ARBITRATION vs Genetics [Medicine]: basic heredity, population/quantitative genetics, genomics methodology, and non-human (animal/plant/livestock) genetics stay here; human clinical genetics, hereditary-disease diagnosis, genetic testing/counseling, and gene-disease association work framed around patient risk belong to Genetics [Medicine].
includes: population and quantitative genetics; genetic epidemiology and GWAS; genomics and genome analysis; heredity and inheritance patterns; forensic genetics; genetic diversity and structure within and between populations of a species; human, animal, and livestock genetics
excludes: molecular/biochemical mechanisms of gene expression and regulation -> Molecular Biology ; evolutionary and ecological processes of genetic variation in natural populations -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; human clinical/medical genetics: hereditary disease diagnosis, genetic testing and counseling, and gene-disease association studies framed around individual patient risk or health outcome -> Genetics
flagship_journals: Nature Genetics; Genetics; American Journal of Human Genetics; PLOS Genetics

scope: The molecular mechanisms underlying gene expression, protein structure and function, and signal transduction at the DNA/RNA/protein level, including transcriptional and translational regulation, RNA biology, and molecular signaling pathways.
includes: gene expression and transcriptional regulation; protein structure-function and protein-protein interactions; signal transduction pathways; RNA biology; epigenetics; molecular mechanisms of disease; receptor and enzyme molecular mechanisms
excludes: whole-cell and organelle-level processes -> Cell Biology ; heredity and population-level genetic variation -> Genetics ; chemistry of metabolism and small-molecule biochemistry -> Biochemistry ; cancer-specific oncogenic mechanisms -> Cancer Research ; drug-receptor pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics -> Pharmacology ; plant-specific molecular processes -> Plant Science
flagship_journals: Molecular Cell; Cell; Nature; EMBO Journal; Journal of Biological Chemistry

scope: Research that applies molecular-biology mechanisms and tools to understand, diagnose, and treat human disease. Covers the translational bridge between basic molecular/cell biology and clinical application: disease-causing molecular pathways, molecular diagnostics and biomarkers, gene- and cell-based therapies, and precision/personalized medicine.
includes: translational research; molecular diagnostics and biomarkers; gene therapy and cell therapy; precision/personalized medicine; molecular pathology of disease; genomic medicine; targeted drug mechanisms; disease models at the molecular level
excludes: basic molecular biology mechanisms with no disease/clinical framing -> Molecular Biology ; normal (non-disease) organ/system function -> Physiology ; cancer-specific molecular biology and oncogenesis -> Cancer Research
flagship_journals: Molecular Medicine; EMBO Molecular Medicine; Trends in Molecular Medicine; Journal of Molecular Medicine

scope: The study of how organisms, organs, tissues, and cells function under normal (non-disease) conditions. Encompasses cellular, systems, comparative, and integrative physiology across cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine, neuromuscular, and exercise domains, in humans and other organisms. ARBITRATION vs Physiology [Medicine]: comparative, cross-species, cellular/systems-mechanism physiology (including non-human organisms) stays here; human, clinical/applied, and non-disease functional-status physiology (nutrition, aging, exercise physiology of patients) belongs to Physiology [Medicine].
includes: cellular and systems physiology; cardiovascular and respiratory physiology; endocrine and metabolic physiology; exercise and environmental physiology; comparative/animal physiology; neurophysiology (systems level); homeostasis and regulatory mechanisms
excludes: disease mechanisms and molecular pathology -> Molecular Medicine ; anatomical structure without functional focus -> Anatomy ; structural/molecular determinants of macromolecule function -> Structural Biology ; human clinical/applied physiology tied directly to organ-system disease management, or physiology research whose framing is a specific patient population or clinical-practice context -> Physiology
flagship_journals: American Journal of Physiology; The Journal of Physiology; Physiological Reviews; Acta Physiologica

scope: The determination and interpretation of the three-dimensional structure of biological macromolecules (proteins, nucleic acids, complexes) and how structure relates to function. Includes experimental structure-determination methods and structure-based mechanistic/functional analysis.
includes: X-ray crystallography; cryo-electron microscopy; NMR of biomolecules; protein structure-function relationships; macromolecular complexes; structural bioinformatics/modeling; membrane protein structure
excludes: purely biophysical/theoretical modeling without structural determination focus -> Biophysics ; sequence-based genomics/genetics without 3D structure focus -> Genetics ; disease-oriented molecular mechanisms -> Molecular Medicine
flagship_journals: Structure; Journal of Structural Biology; Nature Structural & Molecular Biology; Acta Crystallographica Section D

scope: The study of financial and managerial accounting: how organizations measure, record, report, and audit financial information, and how accounting information affects decisions, governance, and markets. Includes financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and management accounting.
includes: financial reporting and disclosure; auditing and assurance; corporate taxation and tax avoidance; managerial/cost accounting; earnings management; corporate governance disclosure; accounting information systems (accounting side)
excludes: investment, asset pricing, and corporate financial decisions -> Finance ; overall firm strategy and competitive positioning -> Strategy and Management
flagship_journals: The Accounting Review; Journal of Accounting Research; Journal of Accounting and Economics; Accounting, Organizations and Society

scope: Management research with a cross-border, comparative, or global dimension: multinational enterprise strategy, international business operations, cross-cultural management, and comparative management systems across countries.
includes: multinational enterprise (MNE) strategy; international market entry and expansion; cross-cultural management; global supply chain and operations management; comparative management practices across countries; foreign direct investment; international trade management
excludes: single-country/domestic firm strategy and general management practice with no cross-border, comparative, or global dimension -> Strategy and Management ; management, marketing, and operations of the tourism, travel, or hospitality industries, even when studied cross-nationally -> Tourism, Leisure and Hospitality Management ; employment relations, collective bargaining, and labor-management negotiation, even in a multinational or comparative setting -> Industrial relations ; macro-level economic growth, trade theory, and econometric modeling of cross-country economic phenomena, where economics rather than firm-level management strategy is the object -> Economics and Econometrics ; the sociological study of organizations, work, and economic life as social institutions, rather than the applied cross-border management-strategy question -> Sociology and Political Science
flagship_journals: Journal of International Business Studies; International Business Review; Journal of World Business

scope: The management, adoption, and organizational impact of information systems and digital technologies within firms. Covers enterprise systems, business intelligence and analytics, IT governance and value, digital transformation, and technology-enabled supply chain/operations management.
includes: ERP systems implementation; business intelligence and big data analytics (business use); IT governance and IT value; e-business/digital transformation; supply chain and operations technology adoption; outsourcing of IT/business processes; decision support systems
excludes: core computer-science development of information-system technologies/algorithms -> Information Systems ; supply chain/inventory operations research without an IS/technology focus -> Management Science and Operations Research
flagship_journals: MIS Quarterly; Information Systems Research; Journal of Management Information Systems; European Journal of Information Systems

scope: The management of innovation processes and technological change within and across organizations: how firms generate, adopt, and commercialize new technologies and products, and how innovation is organized, funded, and diffused.
includes: R&D management; innovation strategy and processes; technology adoption and diffusion; new product development; open innovation and technology transfer; innovation ecosystems and entrepreneurship; patents and technology commercialization (management view)
excludes: macro-level economics of innovation and technological change -> Economics and Econometrics ; general corporate strategy without a technology/innovation focus -> Strategy and Management
flagship_journals: Research Policy; Technovation; Journal of Product Innovation Management; IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management

scope: The study of how firms create, communicate, and deliver value to customers, and how consumers perceive, choose, and respond to products, brands, and prices. Covers consumer behavior, marketing strategy, branding and advertising, market research, and retail.
includes: consumer behavior and decision-making; branding and advertising; pricing and market research; retail and channel management; digital/social media marketing; sustainability and marketing; packaging and product perception
excludes: economic/econometric modeling of consumer choice without a marketing-management lens -> Economics and Econometrics
flagship_journals: Journal of Marketing; Journal of Consumer Research; Journal of Marketing Research; Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

subfield_name: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management
scope: The study of individual and group behavior within organizations, and the management of people through HR practices. Covers leadership, motivation, job attitudes, organizational culture and change, and human resource functions such as recruitment, training, performance, and talent management.
includes: leadership and management style; job satisfaction and employee motivation; organizational culture and change; human resource management and talent management; organizational learning; teams and group dynamics; workplace diversity and well-being
excludes: firm-level competitive strategy and corporate-level decisions -> Strategy and Management
flagship_journals: Journal of Applied Psychology; Academy of Management Journal; Human Resource Management Journal; Journal of Organizational Behavior

scope: The study of firm-level strategy, competitive advantage, and general management: how organizations formulate and execute strategy, compete, grow, and govern themselves. Includes corporate strategy, competitive analysis, knowledge management, and broad management topics not specific to a functional area (marketing, HR, accounting, IS).
includes: corporate and competitive strategy; business model innovation; knowledge management; corporate governance (strategic view); mergers, acquisitions and diversification; entrepreneurship at firm-strategy level; general management topics; corporate social responsibility, business ethics and sustainability strategy as firm management
excludes: employee-level behavior, leadership style, and HR practices -> Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management ; technology/innovation-specific management -> Management of Technology and Innovation ; financial reporting and accounting practices -> Accounting ; environmental regulation, impact assessment and environmental policy instruments as the object -> Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law
flagship_journals: Strategic Management Journal; Academy of Management Review; Journal of Management; Long Range Planning

scope: Management and business research on the tourism, travel, hospitality, and leisure industries: hotel and restaurant management, destination management and marketing, tourist behavior, and leisure/recreation management.
includes: hotel and hospitality management; destination marketing and management; tourist behavior and experience; leisure and recreation management; sustainable tourism and ecotourism; events and MICE tourism; hospitality operations and service quality
excludes: general international/cross-border management strategy not specific to the tourism, travel, or hospitality industries -> Business and International Management ; employment relations, collective bargaining, and labor-management negotiation within the tourism/hospitality workforce -> Industrial relations ; geographic/spatial analysis of destinations, travel flows, and tourism regions, where geographic method rather than management/marketing framing is the object -> Geography, Planning and Development ; macro-level economic analysis of tourism's contribution to national accounts, trade, or growth, treated as economics rather than industry management -> Economics and Econometrics ; the sociological study of tourism, leisure, and travel as consumption practice and social behavior, rather than as industry management and marketing -> Sociology and Political Science
flagship_journals: Tourism Management; Annals of Tourism Research; Journal of Sustainable Tourism; International Journal of Hospitality Management

scope: The study of employment relationships between employers, employees, and their collective representatives: labor unions, collective bargaining, workplace conflict, labor law and policy, and employment negotiation systems.
includes: collective bargaining and trade unions; labor-management relations; labor law and policy; strikes and industrial conflict; workplace dispute resolution; employment negotiation; comparative labor relations systems
excludes: general cross-border management strategy and business operations without a labor/employment-relations focus -> Business and International Management ; individual-level organizational behavior and human-resource practices (recruitment, performance management, motivation) not focused on collective bargaining or union relations -> Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management ; doctrinal analysis of labor statutes, case law, and legal frameworks as an object of legal scholarship -> Law ; broad sociological theory of class, work, and social structure not focused on the specific institutional mechanics of unions, collective bargaining, or labor law -> Sociology and Political Science
flagship_journals: British Journal of Industrial Relations; Industrial Relations: A Journal of Economy and Society; Industrial and Labor Relations Review

scope: The chemical-engineering side of biological engineering: the design and analysis of bioprocesses and bio-based production systems. Covers bioreactors and fermentation, downstream bioprocessing, biocatalysis at process scale, and biomolecular/metabolic engineering for industrial production.
includes: bioreactor and fermentation design; downstream bioprocessing and bioseparations; metabolic and biomolecular engineering; biofuel and bio-based chemical production processes; enzyme/biocatalytic process engineering; tissue/cell culture bioprocessing at scale
excludes: medical devices, implants, biomechanics, and diagnostic/imaging technology -> Biomedical Engineering ; catalytic chemistry and catalyst design not centered on bioprocesses -> Catalysis ; fuel properties, upgrading, and combustion behavior of biofuels (as opposed to the bioprocess/production engineering of making them) -> Fuel Technology
flagship_journals: Biotechnology and Bioengineering; Bioprocess and Biosystems Engineering; Journal of Biotechnology; Biochemical Engineering Journal

scope: The study and engineering of catalytic materials and catalytic reaction processes: how catalysts are designed, characterized, and applied to accelerate and control chemical reactions at bench and industrial scale. Includes heterogeneous, homogeneous, and enzymatic catalysis and catalytic reactor/process engineering.
includes: heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis; catalyst synthesis and characterization; catalytic reaction mechanisms and kinetics; catalytic reactor design; photocatalysis and electrocatalysis (process view); catalysis for energy/fuel conversion
excludes: catalytic nanomaterials/nanoparticles designed for drug delivery or in-body biomedical devices -> Biomedical Engineering ; bioprocess-scale biocatalysis and fermentation -> Bioengineering
flagship_journals: Journal of Catalysis; Applied Catalysis B: Environmental; ACS Catalysis; Catalysis Today

scope: The study of health, safety, and hazard management in the handling, processing, and industrial use of chemicals. Covers process safety, hazard and risk analysis, chemical exposure and toxicity in occupational settings, and regulatory/hygiene practice for chemical operations.
includes: process safety and hazard analysis; chemical exposure and occupational toxicology; accident/incident analysis in chemical plants; risk assessment for chemical processes; chemical hygiene and regulatory compliance; loss prevention engineering
excludes: general environmental/ecological toxicology unrelated to industrial process safety -> Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis
flagship_journals: Journal of Loss Prevention in the Process Industries; Process Safety and Environmental Protection; Journal of Hazardous Materials

scope: The engineering of processes that separate mixtures into components at bench and industrial scale. Covers filtration, membrane separation, distillation, extraction, adsorption, and particle/solid-liquid separation, including the equipment and process design for these operations.
includes: membrane separation and filtration; distillation and extraction; adsorption processes; particle and solid-liquid separation; crystallization as a separation step; process-scale chromatography
excludes: analytical-scale chromatography used for chemical analysis/identification -> Analytical Chemistry ; general fluid transport phenomena not tied to a separation operation -> Fluid Flow and Transfer Processes
flagship_journals: Separation and Purification Technology; Journal of Membrane Science; Chemical Engineering Research and Design

scope: The study of transport phenomena in chemical engineering systems: fluid flow, heat transfer, and mass transfer, including multiphase flow and their coupling in reactors and process equipment. Covers both fundamental transport theory and its application to process design.
includes: fluid mechanics in process equipment; heat transfer in reactors and exchangers; mass transfer operations; multiphase and granular flow; computational fluid dynamics for process systems; momentum/energy/mass transport coupling
excludes: separation-specific unit operations (membranes, distillation, filtration) -> Filtration and Separation ; general/aerospace/mechanical fluid dynamics without a chemical-process context -> Mechanical Engineering
flagship_journals: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer; Chemical Engineering Science; AIChE Journal; Powder Technology

scope: The industrial and process-scale side of chemical engineering: how chemical transformations are designed, scaled up, and run as production processes. Covers reaction engineering, separation and purification processes, process design/simulation/optimization, and plant-level operation and safety.
includes: reaction engineering; separation processes (distillation, extraction, membrane separation); process design, simulation and optimization; process intensification and scale-up; industrial/applied catalysis at process scale; chemical plant and process safety; green/sustainable process technology
excludes: molecular-level catalyst design and mechanism studies -> Physical and Theoretical Chemistry ; materials synthesis and characterization as an end in itself -> Materials Chemistry
flagship_journals: Chemical Engineering Science; Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research; Chemical Engineering Journal; Process Safety and Environmental Protection

scope: Development and application of methods and instrumentation to detect, separate, and quantify chemical species in complex samples. Spans chromatography, electroanalytical and sensor-based methods, sample preparation, and analytical method validation across environmental, biological, pharmaceutical, and materials samples.
includes: chromatography (GC, LC, HPLC); mass spectrometry used for quantification/identification; chemical and biosensors; electroanalytical/voltammetric methods; sample preparation and extraction techniques; chemometrics and analytical data processing; method validation and quality control; trace and residue analysis
excludes: structure elucidation where a spectroscopic technique itself is the research focus -> Spectroscopy ; electrochemical energy conversion/storage research (batteries, fuel cells, corrosion) -> Electrochemistry ; synthesis of new organic or inorganic compounds -> Organic Chemistry
flagship_journals: Analytical Chemistry; Analytica Chimica Acta; Talanta; Journal of Chromatography A

scope: Chemistry of electron-transfer processes at electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Covers energy storage and conversion devices, electrocatalysis, corrosion, and electrodeposition, as well as the fundamental electrochemical mechanisms behind them.
includes: batteries and other energy storage electrochemistry; fuel cells and electrolyzers; electrocatalysis; corrosion science and protection; electrodeposition and electroplating; supercapacitors; electrode materials and interfaces; electrochemical sensor mechanisms
excludes: routine use of electroanalytical techniques purely for sample quantification -> Analytical Chemistry ; battery/electrode materials research focused on bulk materials structure rather than electrochemical function -> Materials Chemistry ; energy-storage system and grid-integration engineering (battery pack/module design, battery management systems, grid-scale storage integration) as opposed to the electrochemical mechanism itself -> Energy Engineering and Power Technology ; alloy microstructure and metallurgical-processing-centric corrosion studies (as opposed to mechanism-centric corrosion/protection chemistry) -> Metals and Alloys
flagship_journals: Journal of the Electrochemical Society; Electrochimica Acta; Journal of Power Sources; Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry

scope: Chemistry of inorganic and organometallic compounds, including their synthesis, structure, bonding, and reactivity. Covers coordination chemistry, main-group element chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry, and molecular metal-complex catalysts. ARBITRATION vs Drug Discovery [Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics]: this card owns the fundamental synthesis, structure, and reactivity chemistry of metal/coordination compounds; metal-based compounds designed and evaluated as candidate therapeutic drugs belong to Drug Discovery (3002).
includes: coordination chemistry; organometallic chemistry; main-group element chemistry; bioinorganic chemistry; metal complex synthesis and reactivity; inorganic reaction mechanisms; metal cluster chemistry
excludes: carbon-based molecule synthesis with no metal-centered focus -> Organic Chemistry ; bulk/solid-state inorganic materials engineered for a functional property (semiconductors, ceramics, nanomaterials) -> Materials Chemistry ; metal-based compounds designed and optimized as therapeutic drug candidates (metal-drug design, structure-activity work aimed at discovering a therapeutic agent) -> Drug Discovery
flagship_journals: Inorganic Chemistry; Dalton Transactions; Journal of Organometallic Chemistry; Coordination Chemistry Reviews

scope: Study, synthesis, and reactivity of carbon-based compounds. Covers synthetic methodology, total synthesis, heterocyclic and natural-product chemistry, and synthesis-and-evaluation work that stops short of dedicated medicinal chemistry.
includes: total synthesis; synthetic methodology development; heterocyclic chemistry; natural product synthesis and isolation; organocatalysis; stereochemistry; structure-activity relationship synthesis; organophosphorus/organosulfur chemistry
excludes: metal-centered coordination/organometallic compounds studied for their own bonding and structure -> Inorganic Chemistry ; bulk or functional materials synthesis (polymers as materials, nanomaterials) -> Materials Chemistry ; papers whose core contribution is drug design, structure-activity relationship (SAR), or target-driven medicinal chemistry, where synthesis is a means to that end rather than the contribution itself -> Drug Discovery
flagship_journals: Journal of the American Chemical Society; Organic Letters; Angewandte Chemie; Journal of Organic Chemistry

scope: Fundamental physical and computational study of chemical systems: how molecules are structured, bonded, and how they react and transform, described through theory, computation, and physical measurement.
includes: quantum and computational chemistry; chemical kinetics; chemical thermodynamics; molecular dynamics simulation; statistical mechanics of chemical systems; reaction mechanism theory; density functional theory (DFT) studies
excludes: experimental structure determination where a spectroscopic technique is the primary output -> Spectroscopy ; electron-transfer/electrode-centered electrochemical systems -> Electrochemistry
flagship_journals: Journal of Physical Chemistry A/B; Journal of Chemical Physics; Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics; Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

scope: Use of spectroscopic methods to probe molecular structure, dynamics, and composition. Covers NMR, IR/Raman, UV-Vis/fluorescence, and chiroptical techniques where the spectroscopic method and the structural insight it yields are the research focus.
includes: NMR spectroscopy; IR and Raman spectroscopy; UV-Vis and fluorescence spectroscopy; chiroptical/circular dichroism methods; spectroscopic structure elucidation; spectroscopic instrumentation and technique development
excludes: routine quantitative analysis or method validation using spectroscopic instruments -> Analytical Chemistry ; purely computational prediction of spectra without experimental measurement -> Physical and Theoretical Chemistry
flagship_journals: Journal of Molecular Spectroscopy; Spectrochimica Acta Part A; Applied Spectroscopy; Journal of Raman Spectroscopy

scope: Research on the theory, algorithms, and methods for building systems that learn, reason, or act intelligently: machine learning and deep learning, neural network architectures, statistical and computational modeling of learning, knowledge representation and reasoning, search and planning, and general-purpose learning methods (including graph learning, topic modeling, and data-driven modeling with tools like R/Python). Because AI methods are used across nearly every discipline, this subfield covers the methodological/algorithmic core rather than every domain where AI is applied. ARBITRATION vs Computational Theory and Mathematics [Computer Science]: metaheuristic and evolutionary-computation search algorithms are named here as their home; pure computational-complexity/algorithmic theory without a learning/search-heuristic component stays in Computational Theory and Mathematics (1703).
includes: machine learning and deep learning algorithms; neural network architectures (including graph neural networks); statistical and computational learning theory; knowledge representation and automated reasoning; search, planning and optimization for intelligent agents; topic modeling and unsupervised learning; core natural language processing algorithms; metaheuristic and evolutionary-computation algorithms (genetic algorithms, swarm/nature-inspired optimization) as general-purpose search and optimization methods
excludes: business/enterprise information systems, decision support and IS management applications of AI -> Information Systems ; image- and video-specific tasks (classification, detection, segmentation) even when solved with AI methods -> Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition ; AI/ML methods applied as a tool within genomics, proteomics or other molecular-biology research questions -> Molecular Biology ; pure computational complexity and algorithmic theory without a learning/AI component -> Computational Theory and Mathematics ; classical and learning-free control theory and dynamical systems control -> Control and Systems Engineering ; general statistical data-analysis methodology and statistical software practice with no learning/AI contribution -> Statistics and Probability
flagship_journals: Artificial Intelligence; Journal of Machine Learning Research; Machine Learning; IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems; Artificial Intelligence Review

scope: Theoretical foundations of computing and discrete mathematics as applied to computation: what can be computed, how efficiently, and the mathematical structures (graphs, automata, algebraic structures) underlying algorithms. ARBITRATION vs Management Science and Operations Research [Decision Sciences] and Artificial Intelligence [Computer Science]: this card owns the mathematical/algorithmic theory of combinatorial optimization (complexity, graph/discrete structures, exact algorithms); decision-oriented applied optimization for management/operations belongs to Management Science and Operations Research (1803); metaheuristic and evolutionary search methods belong to Artificial Intelligence (1702).
includes: computational complexity theory; algorithm design and analysis; graph theory; combinatorics and combinatorial optimization; automata and formal language theory; cellular automata; discrete mathematics; matrix and numerical algorithm theory
excludes: machine learning model design and learning algorithms -> Artificial Intelligence ; optimization framed as management/operational decision-making methodology (applied operations research, logistics, scheduling, resource allocation) rather than the mathematical/algorithmic structure of the problem -> Management Science and Operations Research ; metaheuristic and evolutionary-computation algorithms (genetic algorithms, swarm/nature-inspired optimization) as general-purpose learning/search methods -> Artificial Intelligence
flagship_journals: Theoretical Computer Science; SIAM Journal on Computing; Journal of Computer and System Sciences; Discrete Mathematics

scope: Generation, manipulation, and rendering of visual and geometric digital content, plus computer-aided tools for engineering design. Covers 3D modeling and rendering, animation, geometric/solid modeling, and CAD/CAM systems.
includes: 3D rendering and modeling; computer animation; geometric and solid modeling; CAD/CAM systems; scientific and data visualization; virtual reality graphics pipelines; mesh processing
excludes: analysis or recognition of existing visual/image data -> Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition ; interface and interaction design of graphical systems, where the user experience is the focus -> Human-Computer Interaction
flagship_journals: ACM Transactions on Graphics; Computer Graphics Forum; Computer-Aided Design; IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics

scope: Design, protocols, and performance of computer and communication networks, from wired and wireless infrastructure to mobile, ad-hoc, and IoT connectivity. Covers network architecture, routing, security, and quality-of-service, at the protocol/systems level rather than the physical-layer hardware level.
includes: network protocols and architecture; wireless and mobile networking; wireless sensor networks; IoT connectivity; network security; routing and quality of service (QoS); cellular/5G networking (protocol and systems aspects)
excludes: physical-layer hardware, antenna, or signal-processing design of communication systems -> Electrical and Electronic Engineering ; enterprise or organizational information-systems use of networked infrastructure -> Information Systems
flagship_journals: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking; Computer Networks; IEEE Communications Magazine; Ad Hoc Networks

scope: Application of computer science methods and software to specific domains and industries where the contribution is a computational tool or system for that domain, rather than a novel CS-theoretical, networking, or AI/vision contribution belonging to a more specific subfield. Functions as the applied/domain-crossing bucket within Computer Science. NOTE: ASJC has no bioinformatics or computational-biology subfield. This card is their de-facto home when the contribution is the computational method or tool; when the contribution is the biological finding, classify by the biology.
includes: domain-specific computational tools and software; applied algorithms for a specific industry or discipline; computational methods supporting other scientific/engineering fields; software application development; digital tools built for non-CS disciplines; bioinformatics and computational-biology tooling: sequence analysis, annotation pipelines, biomedical text mining and ontologies
excludes: enterprise/organizational IT systems and their design or deployment -> Information Systems ; decision support systems and IT governance as managerial objects -> Information Systems and Management
flagship_journals: Journal of Computational Science; Expert Systems with Applications

scope: Extraction, interpretation, and recognition of information from visual data such as images and video. Covers image processing, object/face/scene recognition, image classification and retrieval, and pattern recognition applied to visual data, including deep-learning methods specifically for vision tasks.
includes: image processing and enhancement; object, face and scene recognition; image classification and segmentation; image/video retrieval; pattern recognition on visual data; deep learning architectures for vision tasks
excludes: general machine-learning theory/algorithms not specific to visual data -> Artificial Intelligence ; 1-D signal/audio processing and general signal-processing theory -> Signal Processing ; pattern recognition on non-visual sensor streams (accelerometer, wearable, physiological time series) where no image or video is involved -> Signal Processing
flagship_journals: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence; International Journal of Computer Vision; Computer Vision and Image Understanding; Pattern Recognition

scope: Design and organization of computer hardware and system architecture. Covers processor/computer architecture, embedded systems, parallel and distributed computing hardware, digital circuit design for computing, and hardware-software co-design.
includes: computer architecture; embedded systems design; parallel and distributed computing systems; VLSI and digital circuit design; memory and storage systems; hardware-software co-design; FPGA/ASIC design
excludes: analog electronics or general electrical circuit theory not tied to computing systems -> Electrical and Electronic Engineering
flagship_journals: IEEE Transactions on Computers; ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization; Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing; IEEE Micro

scope: Design, evaluation, and understanding of the interaction between people and computing systems. Covers usability and user-experience research, interaction techniques (touch, gesture, gaze, voice), accessibility, and immersive or wearable interfaces, wherever the user's experience of the interaction is the focus. ARBITRATION vs Human Factors and Ergonomics [Social Sciences] and Communication [Social Sciences]: this card owns interface/interaction-technique design and user experience of computing systems; Human Factors and Ergonomics owns workplace/organizational human-system performance beyond the computing interface; Communication owns computer-mediated communication as behavior, content and social process.
includes: usability and UX research; user interface design and evaluation; interaction techniques (gesture, gaze, touch, voice); accessibility and assistive technology; virtual/augmented reality interfaces; wearable interaction devices; user studies
excludes: underlying rendering/graphics-pipeline technology without an interaction or user-experience focus -> Computer Graphics and Computer-Aided Design ; computer-vision recognition algorithms not centered on user interaction -> Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition ; workplace ergonomics, workload and human performance in socio-technical systems beyond the computing interface -> Human Factors and Ergonomics ; computer-mediated communication studied as communication behavior, content, and social process (message content, media effects, social use of communication technology), as opposed to the interface/interaction-technique design itself -> Communication
flagship_journals: International Journal of Human-Computer Studies; ACM Transactions on Computer-Human Interaction; Interacting with Computers

scope: Information Systems studies how organizations and societies design, adopt, manage, and use information and communication technologies to support business processes, decision-making, and social or community goals. It covers information system development and management, information retrieval and behavior, and the deployment of ICT in specific social contexts such as government, education-adjacent community services, and developing regions, treating technology in its organizational and human-use context rather than as pure algorithms or network infrastructure. ARBITRATION vs Library and Information Sciences [3309]: the technical design, engineering, and organizational deployment/management of information systems stays here; the social-science study of library/archival practice, information behavior, and scholarly-communication metrics goes to Library and Information Sciences. ARBITRATION vs Information Systems and Management [Decision Sciences] and Management Information Systems [Business]: the design, engineering and societal deployment of information systems stays here; managerial adoption, governance, decision support and organisational impact go to Information Systems and Management; firm-level MIS and e-business go to Management Information Systems.
includes: information systems development and management; e-government and digital public services; ICT for development (ICT4D); information retrieval and search behavior; digital and cyber forensics; enterprise and organizational information systems; information behavior and user studies; mobile and ubiquitous information technologies and their adoption
excludes: educational technology and e-learning pedagogy -> Education ; machine learning and AI algorithms/methods themselves -> Artificial Intelligence ; network protocols and communications infrastructure -> Computer Networks and Communications ; general applied computing techniques not tied to organizational/social IS use -> Computer Science Applications ; the social-science study of library and archival practice, information behavior as a scholarly discipline, and bibliometrics/scientometrics -> Library and Information Sciences ; strategic, managerial and organisational-impact questions of IS in firms - IT governance, IS adoption, decision support, business informatics -> Information Systems and Management ; firm-level management information systems and e-business studied from a business-school perspective -> Management Information Systems
flagship_journals: MIS Quarterly; Information Systems Research; Journal of Management Information Systems; Information & Management; European Journal of Information Systems

scope: Signal Processing covers the theory and methods for acquiring, analyzing, filtering, transforming, and reconstructing one-dimensional and sensor-based signals (audio, speech, biomedical, communications) using digital and analog techniques. It includes speech and audio processing, filter design, time-frequency analysis, and compression, focused on the signal itself rather than on visual/image pattern recognition.
includes: speech and audio processing; digital filter design; time-frequency and wavelet analysis; signal compression and coding; biomedical and sensor signal processing; adaptive and statistical signal processing; array and radar signal processing
excludes: image and video pattern recognition/classification -> Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition ; biosensor, medical-device and imaging-hardware engineering where the physical sensing system rather than the signal algorithm is the contribution -> Biomedical Engineering
flagship_journals: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing; Signal Processing; IEEE Signal Processing Letters; Digital Signal Processing; Speech Communication

scope: Software covers the engineering, construction, testing, verification, and maintenance of software systems, including software design methodologies, programming paradigms, software quality and reliability, and end-user or no-code computing tools. It centers on how software is built and assured rather than on any specific application domain.
includes: software engineering and design methodologies; software testing and debugging; software reliability and quality assurance; model-driven and formal software development; programming languages and paradigms; end-user computing and spreadsheets; software maintenance and evolution
excludes: business/enterprise information-systems design, deployment, and organizational IT management, as opposed to the software engineering/construction discipline itself -> Information Systems ; machine-learning/AI algorithm design and model development, as opposed to the software-engineering process used to build and assure the system -> Artificial Intelligence ; network protocol design, distributed-systems communication, and network architecture, as opposed to general software construction, testing, and maintenance -> Computer Networks and Communications ; feedback-control and systems-engineering theory applied to physical or embedded systems, as opposed to general-purpose software construction -> Control and Systems Engineering
flagship_journals: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering; ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology; Journal of Systems and Software; Empirical Software Engineering

scope: Last-resort bucket for decision-sciences research that is broad or cross-cutting and does not fit specifically into Information Systems and Management, Management Science and Operations Research, or Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty. Covers general decision theory, judgment and decision-making, and interdisciplinary decision-support scholarship.
includes: general decision theory; judgment and decision-making; decision support frameworks (general); risk and uncertainty in decision-making (non-statistical); multi-criteria decision analysis (general); behavioral decision research; decision science pedagogy
flagship_journals: Decision Sciences

scope: Information Systems and Management addresses the strategic, organizational, and managerial dimensions of information systems within business and decision-making contexts, including decision support systems, IT governance, business informatics, and the management of information resources as drivers of organizational performance. ARBITRATION: this card requires an information-systems object; general management, open-science, team-science or accountability topics without IS content do not belong here.
includes: decision support systems; IT governance and IS strategy; business informatics; knowledge management systems; enterprise information management; IS adoption and organizational impact; management information systems
excludes: purely technical/algorithmic information-systems research (retrieval, forensics, ICT4D) not framed managerially -> Information Systems ; technical design, engineering and societal deployment of information systems (e-government, ICT4D, information retrieval) -> Information Systems ; general management, strategy or organisational research with no information-systems content -> Strategy and Management
