flagship_journals: Information & Management; Decision Support Systems; Journal of Strategic Information Systems; Information Systems Management

scope: Management Science and Operations Research applies mathematical modeling, optimization, and quantitative decision-making methods to management and organizational problems. It spans multi-criteria decision analysis, risk and portfolio optimization, fuzzy and soft set theory, complex-systems decision modeling. ARBITRATION vs Computational Theory and Mathematics [Computer Science]: this card owns optimization and decision methodology applied to management/operational problems; the mathematical/algorithmic theory of combinatorial optimization as a computer-science topic belongs to Computational Theory and Mathematics (1703).
includes: operations research and optimization; multi-criteria decision making; risk and portfolio optimization; fuzzy and soft set theory; complex systems and decision modeling; simulation and stochastic modeling; structured and multi-criteria decision methods; supply chain and logistics optimization
excludes: general probability theory and statistical inference methodology developed and evaluated as statistics research in its own right, without a management/operational decision-optimization framing -> Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty ; decision-support and information-systems-strategy questions framed around organizational/managerial IT governance rather than mathematical optimization or OR methodology -> Information Systems and Management ; production-floor and manufacturing-system operations research (scheduling, factory automation, process optimization) framed as industrial/manufacturing engineering practice -> Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering ; the mathematical/algorithmic theory of combinatorial optimization (complexity analysis, graph-theoretic and discrete-structure results) developed as computer-science theory rather than a management/operational decision application -> Computational Theory and Mathematics
flagship_journals: Management Science; Operations Research; European Journal of Operational Research; Omega; Decision Sciences

scope: Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty covers statistical theory, probabilistic modeling, and methods for quantifying and managing uncertainty and measurement error, applied to decision-relevant contexts. It includes uncertainty evaluation in scientific measurement alongside general probability and statistical methodology used to inform decisions under uncertainty. ARBITRATION vs Statistics and Probability [Mathematics]: this card owns decision-relevant applied statistics and uncertainty quantification; pure mathematical statistical theory pursued as mathematics scholarship belongs to Statistics and Probability (2613).
includes: probability theory; statistical inference and modeling; uncertainty quantification; measurement error and metrology statistics; stochastic processes; applied statistics for decision-making; Bayesian and frequentist methods
excludes: quantitative uncertainty modeling used as an input to an optimization or operational decision problem, where the operations-research/decision-modeling framing is the actual contribution -> Management Science and Operations Research ; pure mathematical statistical theory (proofs, foundational probability theory) pursued as mathematics scholarship rather than decision-relevant applied statistics -> Statistics and Probability ; statistical/probabilistic methodology developed specifically to support machine-learning model design and training -> Artificial Intelligence
flagship_journals: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society; The Annals of Statistics; Statistics & Probability Letters; Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference

scope: The broad, generalist practice and science of dentistry and oral health, covering topics that span multiple dental specialties or do not fit a single specialty subfield. As a 'General' bucket, this is the last-resort home for dentistry topics that are cross-cutting (e.g., general oral health, dental education, dental public health, dental materials science broadly) rather than specific to surgery, orthodontics, or periodontics.
includes: general/family dentistry; oral health and hygiene; dental education and training; dental public health and epidemiology; dental materials (general); preventive dentistry; restorative dentistry; cross-specialty dental topics
excludes: tooth extraction, implants, and maxillofacial surgery -> Oral Surgery ; malocclusion and orthodontic appliances -> Orthodontics ; gum disease and periodontal treatment -> Periodontics
flagship_journals: Journal of the American Dental Association; British Dental Journal; Community Dentistry and Oral Epidemiology

scope: Surgical and interventional dental care: tooth extractions, dental implants, jaw and maxillofacial surgery, endodontic (root canal) procedures, and dental/oral imaging used to plan and evaluate these interventions.
includes: dental implants; tooth extraction; maxillofacial surgery; endodontics/root canal treatment; dental/oral radiography and imaging; oral pathology surgery; anesthesia in dental surgery
excludes: tooth alignment and bite correction -> Orthodontics ; gum and supporting-tissue disease treatment -> Periodontics
flagship_journals: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery; International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery; Clinical Oral Implants Research

scope: The diagnosis, prevention, and correction of malpositioned teeth and jaws (malocclusion), including the design and use of braces, aligners, and other orthodontic appliances, as well as dentofacial orthopedics.
includes: malocclusion correction; braces and clear aligners; dentofacial orthopedics; orthodontic appliance design; bite/occlusion analysis; dental materials and restorations related to alignment

ARBITRATION vs Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty [Decision Sciences]: this card owns statistics and probability theory and methodology pursued as mathematics/statistics scholarship in its own right; decision-oriented applied statistics and uncertainty quantification framed for management/operational decision-making belong to Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty (1804).

scope: Covers the mathematical foundations of computation: algorithms and their complexity, formal models of computation, logic, and the theory underlying programming languages and cryptography.
includes: computational complexity theory; algorithm design and analysis; automata theory and formal languages; computability theory; logic and formal methods in computer science; theoretical cryptography; combinatorial and graph-theoretic algorithms
excludes: applied/systems-level software and computing infrastructure -> Computer Science Applications ; statistical learning theory framed as an AI method -> Artificial Intelligence ; applied security protocols, cryptanalysis of deployed systems and network security engineering -> Computer Networks and Communications

scope: The structural organization of the human (and comparative) body at the gross, microscopic, and developmental level. Covers gross anatomy, histology, neuroanatomy, and comparative/functional anatomy, typically as a descriptive or structural discipline underlying clinical and biological specialties.
includes: gross anatomy and dissection-based studies; histology and microanatomy; neuroanatomy; comparative and functional anatomy; developmental/embryological anatomy; anatomical variation and clinical anatomy for surgical planning
excludes: physiological function and regulation as the primary focus rather than structure -> Physiology

scope: Covers the clinical practice and research of anesthesia, perioperative patient management, sedation, and the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic pain.
includes: general, regional and local anesthesia techniques; perioperative monitoring and management; critical care sedation and analgesia; chronic pain syndromes and management; opioid and non-opioid analgesics; nerve blocks and interventional pain procedures; palliative and cancer pain control
excludes: general or multisystem adult inpatient medicine and comorbidity management where anesthesia or a pain-procedure is not the focus -> Internal Medicine ; ongoing multi-organ critical-illness management in the ICU beyond perioperative anesthesia and procedural analgesia -> Critical Care and Intensive Care Medicine ; the neuroscience mechanism of pain perception, nociceptive processing, or the placebo effect studied without a clinical anesthetic or interventional-pain-procedure framing -> Sensory Systems
flagship_journals: Anesthesiology; Anesthesia & Analgesia; British Journal of Anaesthesia; Pain; Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine

scope: Covers the chemical processes and biomolecules underlying human physiology and disease: metabolism, enzymes, and the structure/function of proteins, lipids, and other biomolecules, especially as studied in a clinical or biomedical context. ARBITRATION vs Biochemistry [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: biochemistry framed around a human disease mechanism, disease biomarker, or clinical/biomedical outcome stays here; fundamental, mechanism-first biomolecule chemistry studied for its own sake (any organism) belongs to Biochemistry [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology].
includes: metabolic pathways and enzyme kinetics; clinical/diagnostic biochemistry; protein, lipid and carbohydrate biochemistry; biomarkers of disease; oxidative stress and redox biochemistry; biochemical basis of disease mechanisms
excludes: gene expression, cell signaling, and molecular genetic mechanisms -> Molecular Biology ; fundamental, non-disease-framed chemistry of biomolecules (enzyme mechanism, metabolic pathway chemistry, bioenergetics) studied for its own biochemical interest rather than a human disease or clinical outcome -> Biochemistry ; laboratory diagnostics, assay methodology and disease-marker measurement as lab medicine -> Clinical Biochemistry
flagship_journals: Journal of Biological Chemistry; Biochemistry; Clinical Biochemistry; Biochemical Journal

scope: Covers clinical and translational research on diseases of the heart and vascular system, including their diagnosis, risk assessment, and treatment.
includes: coronary artery disease and heart failure; cardiac arrhythmias and electrophysiology; hypertension and cardiovascular risk factors; cardiac imaging and diagnostics; interventional and structural cardiology; cardiac devices (pacing, defibrillation); cardiovascular disease in special populations (e.g. pregnancy)
excludes: general or multisystem adult medicine where a cardiovascular abnormality is incidental rather than the primary diagnosis -> Internal Medicine ; basic molecular/genetic mechanisms of cardiac disease (protein aggregation, ion-channel mutation biology) studied without patient-level diagnosis or clinical management -> Molecular Biology ; engineering design and development of cardiac devices (pacemakers, mechanical circulatory support hardware) as a technology contribution -> Biomedical Engineering ; preclinical cardiovascular pharmacology: vasoactive peptides, receptor pharmacology and drug mechanism without patient-level framing -> Pharmacology

flagship_journals: Critical Care Medicine; Intensive Care Medicine; Critical Care; Journal of Critical Care

scope: Covers the clinical practice and research of skin, hair, and nail diseases, including their diagnosis, treatment, and dermatologic manifestations of systemic disease.

scope: Covers research on hormone-producing glands and endocrine disorders, diabetes mellitus, and metabolic disease, including their diagnosis, management, and complications.

flagship_journals: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism; Diabetes Care; Diabetologia; Endocrine Reviews

scope: Covers the study of disease distribution, risk factors, and outcomes across populations, and population-level/clinical-outcomes research spanning acute and chronic conditions of many kinds. ARBITRATION vs Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health [Medicine] and Health Informatics [Medicine]: study design, population-level risk-factor/outcomes analysis, and statistical inference own this card; population policy, prevention programming, and environmental/occupational practice belong to Public Health; health-data-system technology and infrastructure belong to Health Informatics.

excludes: population health policy, environmental/occupational exposure surveillance, and prevention-programme design, as opposed to epidemiologic study design and population-level inference itself -> Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health ; health data systems and informatics infrastructure/technology as the contribution, rather than the epidemiologic study design or statistical population inference -> Health Informatics ; general or multisystem adult clinical medicine where population-level study design is not the contribution -> Internal Medicine ; gene-disease association or heritability analysis as its own contribution, rather than descriptive population incidence or risk-factor analysis -> Genetics

includes: general/family practitioner care; primary care preventive medicine; chronic disease management in primary care; continuity and coordination of care; primary-care doctor-patient communication; community and rural general practice; primary care office procedures

scope: Clinical medicine and pathophysiology of the digestive system: esophagus, stomach, intestines, pancreas, and biliary tract disorders, including endoscopic diagnosis and treatment.
includes: inflammatory bowel disease; GI motility disorders; peptic ulcer and acid-related disease; endoscopy and GI diagnostics; pancreatic and biliary tract disorders; gastrointestinal cancers (clinical); gut microbiome in digestive disease
excludes: liver-specific disease and hepatology -> Hepatology
flagship_journals: Gastroenterology; Gut; American Journal of Gastroenterology; Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology

ARBITRATION vs Genetics [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: clinical/patient-and-disease-framed human genetics (hereditary disorders, genetic testing/counseling, gene-disease association studies aimed at patient risk) stays here; basic heredity, population/quantitative genetics, genomics methodology, and non-human genetics belong to Genetics [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology].
includes: medical and clinical genetics; genetic and hereditary disorders/syndromes; genomics and genome-wide association studies; genetic testing and counseling; gene-disease association studies; population genetics of disease risk
excludes: molecular mechanisms of gene expression/regulation and cell signaling -> Molecular Biology ; evolutionary genetics, phylogenetics and species-level genetic diversity -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics ; population, quantitative, or model-organism genetics research whose object is basic heredity, genomics methodology, or agricultural/livestock genetics rather than human clinical diagnosis, risk, or disease association -> Genetics
flagship_journals: Nature Genetics; American Journal of Human Genetics; Genetics in Medicine; European Journal of Human Genetics

scope: The clinical care and biological/social study of aging and the health of older adults. Covers age-related disease and frailty, geriatric syndromes, care of the elderly across settings, and the clinical (as opposed to purely biological) study of aging.
includes: frailty and functional decline in older adults; geriatric syndromes (falls, delirium, polypharmacy); clinical care models for older adults; aging-related pharmacotherapy and outcomes; long-term and palliative care of the elderly; gerontological epidemiology
excludes: basic biological/molecular mechanisms of aging not framed as clinical geriatric care -> Aging ; general internal medicine not specific to the older-adult population -> Internal Medicine ; social gerontology: ageing as social roles, isolation, cohorts and life transitions rather than clinical care -> Life-span and Life-course Studies
flagship_journals: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society; Age and Ageing; Journal of Gerontology: Medical Sciences

includes: electronic health records; clinical decision support systems; health data analytics; telemedicine and telehealth systems; medical data standards and interoperability; digital health technologies; health information system design

scope: Covers the study of blood, blood-forming organs, and blood-related diseases, including their diagnosis, treatment, and management.
includes: leukemia and lymphoma; anemia and hemoglobinopathies; bleeding and clotting disorders; bone marrow and stem cell transplantation; blood transfusion medicine; myeloproliferative and myelodysplastic disorders

scope: Covers the study of liver, gallbladder, biliary tree, and pancreas diseases, including their diagnosis, treatment, and transplantation.

scope: Clinical medicine of allergic and immune-mediated diseases in patients: diagnosis and treatment of asthma and allergic disease, anaphylaxis, primary immunodeficiency, and clinical allergen immunotherapy. includes: allergic rhinitis and asthma; food allergy and anaphylaxis; allergen immunotherapy; primary immunodeficiency (clinical); urticaria and angioedema; drug allergy; clinical allergy testing and diagnostics

includes: hospitalist and inpatient adult medicine; multisystem or undifferentiated disease diagnosis; general internal medicine practice guidelines; comorbidity management in adults; perioperative internal medicine consultation; internal medicine training and education; general adult preventive care
excludes: a cardiac-defining diagnosis (coronary disease, arrhythmia, heart failure) as the primary contribution -> Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine ; ICU-level multi-organ critical-illness support as the primary contribution -> Critical Care and Intensive Care Medicine ; population-level study design and epidemiologic inference as the contribution -> Epidemiology ; continuous, ambulatory, community-based primary-care practice as the contribution -> Family Practice

scope: Covers infectious agents -- viral, bacterial, fungal, and parasitic -- and the diagnosis, treatment, and clinical management of the diseases they cause.

scope: Clinical/medical microbiology: the diagnosis, laboratory identification, and antimicrobial management of microbial infections in patients, including clinical bacteriology, clinical mycology, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing as practiced in medical and diagnostic-laboratory settings. This is the clinical-practice perspective, distinct from the same-named subfield in the Immunology and Microbiology field, which covers the basic biological science of microorganisms independent of patient care. ARBITRATION vs Microbiology [Immunology and Microbiology]: the clinical-laboratory practice of diagnosing and managing microbial infection in patients (bacteriology/mycology diagnostics, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, hospital infection control) stays here; basic microbial physiology, taxonomy, genetics, ecology, and environmental/industrial microbiology belong to Microbiology [Immunology and Microbiology].
includes: clinical/diagnostic bacteriology; antimicrobial susceptibility testing and stewardship; hospital/healthcare-associated infection microbiology; clinical mycology; microbial diagnostics and laboratory medicine; infection control microbiology; antimicrobial resistance in clinical settings
excludes: basic microbial biology, taxonomy, physiology, and environmental/industrial microbiology not framed around patient diagnosis or treatment -> Microbiology

scope: The medical study, diagnosis, and treatment of the kidneys and the urinary/renal system, including their role in fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base homeostasis. Covers chronic and acute kidney disease, dialysis, and renal complications of systemic disease such as diabetes and hypertension.
includes: chronic kidney disease; acute kidney injury; dialysis and renal replacement therapy; glomerulonephritis and glomerulopathies; diabetic and hypertensive nephropathy; electrolyte and acid-base disorders; renal function testing; hemodialysis vascular access
excludes: kidney transplantation surgery/immunology -> Transplantation ; kidney and urinary tract cancers as oncology entities -> Oncology ; urological surgical procedures (stones, prostate, bladder) -> Urology
flagship_journals: Kidney International; American Journal of Kidney Diseases; Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology; Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation

scope: The clinical medical specialty concerned with diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. ARBITRATION vs Neurology [Neuroscience]: clinical diagnostic and therapeutic practice, patient-management protocols, and health-system-level treatment of neurological disease stay here; translational/mechanistic disease research (pathophysiology, biomarkers, model systems, blood-brain-barrier biology) belongs to Neurology [Neuroscience], even for the same diseases (stroke, epilepsy, neurodegeneration).
includes: stroke and cerebrovascular disease; intracranial aneurysms and vascular malformations; epilepsy and seizure disorders; neurodegenerative disease (Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, ALS) clinical management; peripheral neuropathies; autoimmune and inflammatory neurological disorders; movement disorders; headache and migraine
excludes: basic and cognitive brain function, perception, memory research without clinical disease focus -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; neurosurgical operative procedures -> Surgery ; psychiatric mood/psychotic disorders -> Psychiatry and Mental health ; translational/mechanistic neuroscience research on neurological-disease pathophysiology, disease biomarkers, or model-system studies (e.g. blood-brain-barrier structure/function) where the contribution is disease mechanism rather than patient diagnosis or treatment -> Neurology
flagship_journals: Neurology; Brain; Annals of Neurology; The Lancet Neurology

scope: The medical and surgical care of pregnancy, childbirth, and the female reproductive system. includes: pregnancy and prenatal care; labor, delivery and postpartum complications; maternal-fetal medicine; infertility and reproductive endocrinology; gynecological disorders (endometriosis, fibroids, PCOS); menopause; contraception; gynecological surgery
excludes: gynecological and reproductive cancers as oncology entities -> Oncology ; newborn/infant clinical care after delivery -> Pediatrics, Perinatology and Child Health

excludes: basic molecular/cellular mechanisms of carcinogenesis without clinical framing -> Molecular Biology ; cancer genetics and genomics research -> Genetics ; cancer epidemiology and population risk factors -> Epidemiology ; the physics of radiation dose calculation, source physics, and dosimetry underlying radiotherapy, studied as a physics/engineering discipline rather than clinical oncology practice -> Radiation
flagship_journals: Journal of Clinical Oncology; The Lancet Oncology; Cancer; Annals of Oncology

scope: The medical and surgical specialty dealing with the anatomy, physiology, and diseases of the eye and visual system. Covers diagnosis and treatment of retinal, corneal, and optic nerve disease, glaucoma, cataract, ocular trauma, and vision-related disorders.
includes: glaucoma; retinal and macular disease; cataract surgery; corneal disease; ocular trauma and foreign bodies; optic nerve and neuro-ophthalmic disorders; refractive and laser eye surgery; ocular drug toxicity and pharmacology
excludes: ocular imaging device engineering -> Biomedical Engineering ; ocular tumors as cancer entities -> Oncology
flagship_journals: Ophthalmology; American Journal of Ophthalmology; JAMA Ophthalmology; British Journal of Ophthalmology

scope: The medical and surgical care of the musculoskeletal system, and the clinical science of exercise, athletic performance, and sports-related injury and recovery. includes: fracture and joint injury management; bone health and osteoporosis; joint replacement and arthroplasty; sports injuries and prevention; sports performance and training physiology; spinal and musculoskeletal disorders; biomechanics of movement in a clinical/athletic context; mechanical loading and its effects on musculoskeletal tissue in clinical and athletic contexts; exercise science and physical-activity research framed around musculoskeletal and athletic health
excludes: rehabilitation therapy and functional recovery programs -> Rehabilitation ; bone/soft-tissue tumors as cancer entities -> Oncology
flagship_journals: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery; American Journal of Sports Medicine; British Journal of Sports Medicine; Osteoarthritis and Cartilage

scope: Clinical medicine and surgery of the ear, nose, throat, and related head and neck structures. Covers diagnosis and treatment of hearing and vestibular disorders, sinonasal disease, laryngeal and voice disorders, and head and neck oncologic surgery. ARBITRATION vs Speech and Hearing [Health Professions]: this card owns medical and surgical ENT diagnosis and treatment; non-surgical audiology and speech-language pathology assessment/therapy practice belongs to Speech and Hearing (3616).
includes: ear disease and otitis media; hearing and vestibular disorders; sinusitis and nasal conditions; laryngology and voice disorders; head and neck cancer surgery; pediatric ENT conditions; sleep apnea (ENT-surgical aspects)

flagship_journals: Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery; The Laryngoscope; JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery

scope: Clinical and laboratory pathology (disease mechanisms and tissue/cellular diagnosis via biopsy and autopsy) combined with forensic medicine (medico-legal death investigation, forensic pathology, and forensic science applied to legal proceedings).
includes: anatomic and clinical pathology; histopathology and biopsy diagnosis; autopsy and cause-of-death determination; forensic pathology and medico-legal investigation; forensic toxicology; diagnostic disease-mechanism pathophysiology; cytopathology
excludes: clinical diagnosis and management of disease in a living patient where a tissue/laboratory/autopsy diagnostic procedure is not the contribution -> Internal Medicine ; treatment planning and staging decisions in cancer patients, as opposed to the histopathologic diagnosis itself -> Oncology ; laboratory biomarker or enzyme-assay work not tied to tissue-based histologic or autopsy diagnosis -> Clinical Biochemistry

scope: The clinical care and health of infants, children, and adolescents, including the perinatal period. Covers neonatal and pediatric disease, prenatal and perinatal medicine, child growth and development, and pediatric subspecialty care.

scope: The study of drug action, mechanism, and effects on biological systems: pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, drug discovery, and clinical pharmacotherapy. includes: pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics; clinical development and therapeutic use of new drugs in patients; drug interactions and adverse effects; clinical pharmacotherapy; toxicology of drugs and xenobiotics; pharmacotherapy of drug classes in patient populations; receptor pharmacology; drug delivery mechanisms of action

scope: The study of normal function of the human body's organs, systems, and integrative mechanisms, including how these change with age, nutrition, and physical state. ARBITRATION vs Physiology [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology]: human, clinical/applied, and non-disease functional-status physiology (nutrition, aging, exercise physiology of patients) stays here; comparative, cross-species, and cellular/systems-mechanism physiology belongs to Physiology [Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology].
includes: organ system function (cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine); nutrition and physiology of aging; body composition measurement; thermoregulation and fluid balance; exercise physiology; biophysics of physiological function; circadian and homeostatic regulation
excludes: disease-specific organ pathology and its clinical management [route: the relevant organ-system clinical subfield (e.g. Nephrology, Cardiology)] ; cellular/molecular mechanisms of function -> Physiology
flagship_journals: American Journal of Physiology; Journal of Physiology; Physiological Reviews; Acta Physiologica

scope: The medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis, treatment, and management of mental, mood, and behavioral disorders. Covers psychiatric illness (mood, psychotic, anxiety, personality, and neurodevelopmental disorders), psychiatric pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, and mental health services and outcomes.
includes: mood disorders (depression, bipolar disorder); psychotic disorders (schizophrenia); anxiety and trauma-related disorders; ADHD and neurodevelopmental psychiatric conditions; psychiatric treatment (pharmacotherapy, ECT, psychotherapy); substance use disorders; suicide and self-harm research; mental health services and epidemiology
excludes: basic cognitive/emotional brain mechanisms without clinical psychiatric framing -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; neurological (non-psychiatric) brain disease -> Neurology ; clinical psychology assessment and non-medical psychotherapy research -> Clinical Psychology
flagship_journals: JAMA Psychiatry; American Journal of Psychiatry; The Lancet Psychiatry; Molecular Psychiatry

subfield_name: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
scope: Population-level and preventive health research: public health policy and practice, environmental health hazards and exposures, occupational health and workplace safety, and health-system, ethical, and social dimensions of population health. ARBITRATION vs Epidemiology [Medicine] and Health Informatics [Medicine]: population health policy, prevention programming, and environmental/occupational health practice own this card; epidemiologic study design and population-level inference belong to Epidemiology; health-IT systems and data technology belong to Health Informatics.
includes: public health policy and interventions; environmental health hazards and exposure science; occupational health and workplace safety; health promotion and disease prevention; public health surveillance and monitoring; health equity and social determinants of health; public-health ethics, health law and research governance at population level
excludes: epidemiological study design and methodology as a discipline in itself -> Epidemiology ; health-data-system, digital-health, EHR/informatics technology and its technical implementation, as opposed to population health policy, prevention programming, or environmental/occupational health practice -> Health Informatics ; health inequalities and health-related social policy analysed as social science (sociology/anthropology of health, human rights framing) -> Health ; toxicological mechanism, mutagenesis and dose-response of environmental agents as the object of study -> Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis ; injury and violence prevention framed as safety behaviour, safety culture or risk perception -> Safety Research ; allied-health professions practice, workforce and education -> General Health Professions
flagship_journals: American Journal of Public Health; Environmental Health Perspectives; Occupational and Environmental Medicine; BMC Public Health

scope: Clinical and research medicine of the respiratory system — lungs, airways and pleura — including diagnosis, treatment and pathophysiology of respiratory diseases (asthma, COPD, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary infections, pulmonary vascular disease, sleep-disordered breathing, cystic fibrosis) and lung cancer as a disease of the respiratory organ, together with pulmonary function testing and critical/respiratory intensive care.
includes: obstructive and restrictive lung disease (asthma, COPD, pulmonary fibrosis); lung cancer diagnosis and treatment; pulmonary infections (pneumonia, tuberculosis, other lower respiratory infections); pulmonary vascular disease (pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary embolism); sleep-disordered breathing and sleep medicine; cystic fibrosis and pediatric respiratory disease; pulmonary function testing and respiratory physiology; respiratory critical care and mechanical ventilation
excludes: solid-organ cancers outside the lung (e.g., renal cell carcinoma, prostate cancer) that are not respiratory-organ malignancies -> Oncology ; general diagnostic imaging and pathology technique/technology not specific to the lung -> Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging
flagship_journals: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine; European Respiratory Journal; Chest; Thorax; Lung Cancer

scope: The clinical use of imaging modalities (MRI, CT, ultrasound, nuclear medicine, X-ray, thermography) for diagnosis, staging, and monitoring of disease. Covers clinical imaging protocols, image-based diagnosis, radiation dose and safety, and interventional/nuclear medicine procedures, from the standpoint of clinical application rather than device engineering. ARBITRATION vs Radiation [Physics and Astronomy]: this card owns the clinical/diagnostic use of radiation and imaging, including radiation dose management and radiobiological effects in patient care; the underlying physics of radiation production, propagation, and dosimetry belongs to Radiation (3108).
includes: MRI and CT diagnostic techniques; nuclear medicine and PET imaging; ultrasound diagnostics; radiation dose and imaging safety; image-based cancer diagnosis and staging; interventional radiology procedures; infrared thermography in medicine; contrast agents in clinical imaging
excludes: imaging device/hardware and signal-processing engineering -> Biomedical Engineering ; radiation therapy delivery for cancer treatment -> Oncology ; chemistry and design of radiopharmaceuticals, contrast agents and therapy agents as compounds -> Drug Discovery ; the underlying physics of radiation production, interaction with matter, and dosimetry, studied as a physics/instrumentation discipline rather than clinical application -> Radiation
flagship_journals: Radiology; European Radiology; Journal of Nuclear Medicine; American Journal of Roentgenology

scope: The medical specialty and allied-health practice of restoring function, mobility, and quality of life after injury, illness, surgery, or disability. Covers physical and occupational therapy, rehabilitation medicine protocols, assistive technology use in recovery, and functional outcome assessment.
includes: physical therapy and physiotherapy interventions; occupational therapy; post-surgical and post-injury functional recovery; stroke and neurological rehabilitation; cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation; assistive devices and prosthetics in rehabilitation use; functional and disability outcome measurement
excludes: surgical or pharmacological treatment of the underlying condition [route: the relevant clinical subfield (e.g. Orthopedics and Sports Medicine, Neurology)] ; prosthetic/orthotic device design and engineering -> Biomedical Engineering
flagship_journals: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation; Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine; Disability and Rehabilitation; Clinical Rehabilitation

scope: Clinical and biomedical research on human reproductive function, dysfunction, and treatment across the life course: fertility and infertility, assisted reproductive technologies, andrology, reproductive endocrinology, and reproductive health services. Covers both male and female reproductive systems as a unified clinical specialty.
includes: infertility diagnosis and treatment; assisted reproductive technology (IVF, ICSI, ART); sperm and testicular function; reproductive endocrinology; fertility preservation; andrology; contraception and family planning technologies; reproductive health and technologies
excludes: pregnancy, childbirth, and general gynecologic disease not centered on fertility -> Obstetrics and Gynecology ; male urologic disease outside fertility/andrology (e.g. prostate, bladder, stones) -> Urology ; general endocrine/metabolic disorders unrelated to reproduction -> Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism
flagship_journals: Fertility and Sterility; Human Reproduction; Reproductive Biomedicine Online; Journal of Assisted Reproduction and Genetics

scope: Clinical and translational research on rheumatic, autoimmune, and inflammatory diseases of the joints, connective tissue, and musculoskeletal system, and related systemic autoinflammatory/autoimmune syndromes. Includes bone and joint pathology arising from inflammatory or autoimmune processes, not just classic 'arthritis'.
includes: rheumatoid arthritis and spondyloarthritis; osteoarthritis (medical management); systemic lupus erythematosus and connective tissue disease; vasculitis; autoinflammatory syndromes (e.g. VEXAS, relapsing polychondritis); osteomyelitis and inflammatory bone disorders; bone tumor diagnosis where framed as rheumatologic/osteoarticular disease; gout and crystal arthropathies
excludes: mechanical, traumatic, or sports-related musculoskeletal injury and its surgical management -> Orthopedics and Sports Medicine ; systemic immunology and allergic disease not centered on joints/connective tissue -> Immunology and Allergy
flagship_journals: Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases; Arthritis & Rheumatology; Rheumatology; Seminars in Arthritis and Rheumatism

scope: The broad clinical specialty of operative treatment across body systems: surgical technique, perioperative and postoperative management, surgical complications, and outcomes, spanning general, vascular, gastrointestinal, and other non-organ-specific-specialty operative care. This is a large cross-cutting bucket for operative-care topics not claimed by a more specific surgical/organ subfield.
includes: general and abdominal surgery; surgical site infection and wound management; hernia repair; vascular and aortic surgical conditions; enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols; surgical complications and adhesions; perioperative care; minimally invasive and laparoscopic surgery
excludes: cancer-specific surgical treatment framed around oncologic outcomes -> Oncology ; organ transplantation surgery -> Transplantation ; orthopedic and sports-related surgical procedures -> Orthopedics and Sports Medicine ; obstetric/gynecologic surgery -> Obstetrics and Gynecology
flagship_journals: Annals of Surgery; British Journal of Surgery; JAMA Surgery; Surgery

scope: The medical and surgical science of organ and tissue transplantation: donor and recipient selection, surgical transplantation technique, graft function, immunosuppression, and management of rejection and post-transplant complications.
includes: solid organ transplantation (kidney, liver, heart, lung); hematopoietic stem cell and bone marrow transplantation; graft rejection and immunosuppressive therapy; donor organ preservation and allocation; graft-versus-host disease; post-transplant complications and monitoring
excludes: chronic organ disease management prior to transplant listing [route: the relevant organ-specific subfield (e.g. Nephrology)] ; general immunology mechanisms not specific to transplant rejection -> Immunology
flagship_journals: American Journal of Transplantation; Transplantation; Transplant International; Clinical Transplantation

scope: Clinical medicine and surgery of the urinary tract and male reproductive system. Covers urinary bladder, prostate, kidney (surgical/urologic), and urethral disease and disorders, urologic oncology, and both adult and pediatric urologic care.
includes: urinary bladder and prostate disease; urologic oncology; urinary tract stones and obstruction; male reproductive/urologic disorders; pediatric urology; urodynamics and functional urology
excludes: medical (non-surgical) kidney/renal disease managed as nephrology -> Nephrology ; gross or microscopic anatomy of the urinary/reproductive tract studied for its own sake rather than clinical disease/treatment -> Anatomy
flagship_journals: Journal of Urology; European Urology; Urology

scope: The study of the neural basis of behavior, using primarily animal models and experimental paradigms to link brain circuits, neurotransmitter systems, and neural mechanisms to behavioral output: learning, motivation, emotion, social behavior, and motor action. Bridges basic neurobiology and behavioral/psychological phenomena. ARBITRATION vs Cognitive Neuroscience: human participants studied with neuroimaging or psychophysics go to Cognitive Neuroscience; animal models and behavioural paradigms stay here.
includes: animal models of learning and memory; reward and motivation circuitry; fear, anxiety, and emotional behavior models; neuroendocrine and stress-behavior interactions; social and aggressive behavior neurobiology; addiction and drug-behavior neuroscience; neural circuits underlying motor and instinctive behavior; sleep, arousal and circadian regulation of behaviour; neuropeptide and neuromodulator control of brain states
excludes: human cognitive processes (perception, attention, memory) studied via neuroimaging -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; clinical psychiatric disease framing -> Psychiatry and Mental health ; cellular/molecular neuroscience mechanisms without a behavioral endpoint -> Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
flagship_journals: Behavioral Neuroscience; Neurobiology of Learning and Memory; Psychoneuroendocrinology; Hormones and Behavior

scope: Research into the biological (genetic, neurochemical, neuroimaging, and neuroanatomical) basis of psychiatric disorders. Covers mechanistic and biomarker studies of mental illness in humans and animal models, spanning mood, psychotic, anxiety, and addictive disorders.
includes: neurobiology of depression/anxiety/schizophrenia/bipolar disorder; genetics of psychiatric disease; neuroimaging biomarkers of mental illness; animal models of psychiatric disease; addiction neurobiology; psychoneuroimmunology
excludes: clinical diagnosis, treatment and epidemiology of mental illness -> Psychiatry and Mental health ; general drug mechanism/pharmacodynamics studies not framed around a psychiatric disorder -> Pharmacology
flagship_journals: Biological Psychiatry; Molecular Psychiatry; Neuropsychopharmacology

scope: Study of the nervous system at the cellular and molecular level: neurons, glia, synapses, ion channels, and signaling pathways. Covers mechanisms of neurotransmission, axon guidance, nerve injury/regeneration, and molecular neurobiology across model organisms including invertebrates. ARBITRATION: this card requires the cellular or molecular mechanism ITSELF to be the finding. A systems- or state-level phenomenon (sleep, memory consolidation, circadian behaviour, feeding, addiction, arousal) is classified by its explanandum, not by the technique used - even when studied through identified neurons, receptors or neuropeptides.
includes: synaptic transmission and plasticity mechanisms; ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors; axon guidance and neuronal signaling; glial cell biology; nerve injury and regeneration; molecular/cellular neurobiology in insects and other model organisms
excludes: cognitive- and behavioral-level processing in humans -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; clinical neurological disease diagnosis and treatment -> Neurology ; behavioural or brain-state phenomena (sleep and wakefulness, memory consolidation, circadian behaviour, motivation, addiction) investigated through neuronal or molecular methods - the behavioural endpoint owns the topic -> Behavioral Neuroscience
flagship_journals: Journal of Neuroscience; Neuron; Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience

scope: Study of the neural basis of cognition, perception, and behavior in humans, using neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), psychophysical, and behavioral methods. Covers perception, language, memory, emotion, and aesthetic/musical experience as brain-based processes.
includes: fMRI/EEG studies of cognition; face and object perception; language and bilingualism neuroscience; music and aesthetic perception; memory and learning neuroscience; social and affective neuroscience
excludes: diagnosis, mechanisms and treatment of neurological disease -> Neurology ; cellular/molecular-level mechanisms without a cognitive/behavioral readout -> Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience ; social, affective, or emotional processing where the primary contribution is an individual psychological/behavioral theory of social attitudes, identity, or group processes rather than a brain-imaging/neural-mechanism finding -> Social Psychology
flagship_journals: Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience; NeuroImage; Cortex

scope: Study of nervous system development and change across the lifespan, from neurogenesis and synaptogenesis through neurodevelopmental disorders to brain aging. Includes effects of prenatal/perinatal exposures, anesthesia, or toxins on the developing brain. ARBITRATION: this card requires the DEVELOPMENTAL PROCESS ITSELF to be the object. A clinical neurodevelopmental condition (autism, ADHD, dyslexia) investigated through cognition, behaviour, neuroimaging, genetics, epidemiology or intervention is not developmental neuroscience - route it by its method and framing.
includes: neurogenesis and synaptogenesis; neurodevelopmental disorders studied as disruptions of neural development mechanisms; prenatal and perinatal brain development; developmental neurotoxicity (e.g. anesthesia effects); brain aging and senescence
excludes: adult cellular/molecular signaling mechanisms without a developmental framing -> Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience ; neurodevelopmental conditions studied through cognition, perception or neuroimaging -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; neurodevelopmental conditions studied as clinical psychiatric disorders (diagnosis, prevalence, treatment) -> Psychiatry and Mental health ; neurodevelopmental conditions studied through behavioural, educational or social-skills intervention -> Developmental and Educational Psychology
flagship_journals: Developmental Neuroscience; Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience; Neural Development

scope: Study of neuroendocrine regulation and the autonomic nervous system: the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, stress hormones, circadian control, and autonomic regulation of internal organs and behavior.
includes: neuroendocrinology and HPA axis; stress physiology and stress hormones; circadian rhythm regulation; autonomic nervous system control of organs; hormone-behavior interactions
excludes: general endocrine physiology and hormone action not centred on nervous-system regulation -> Endocrinology ; clinical endocrine and metabolic disease management in patients -> Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism
flagship_journals: Psychoneuroendocrinology; Autonomic Neuroscience; Hormones and Behavior

scope: Clinical and translational study of diseases and disorders of the nervous system, including their mechanisms, diagnosis, and treatment. Covers conditions such as stroke, epilepsy, neurodegenerative disease, and disruption of protective structures like the blood-brain barrier. ARBITRATION vs Neurology [Medicine]: translational/mechanistic disease research (pathophysiology, biomarkers, model systems, blood-brain-barrier biology) stays here; clinical diagnostic and therapeutic practice, patient-management protocols, and health-system-level treatment belong to Neurology [Medicine], even for the same diseases (stroke, epilepsy, neurodegeneration).
includes: stroke and cerebrovascular disease; epilepsy and seizure disorders; neurodegenerative disease (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, etc.); blood-brain barrier structure and function; translational neuroscience of neurological disease: pathophysiology, biomarkers and experimental therapeutics; neuromuscular disorders
excludes: healthy/normal cognitive processing and its neuroimaging correlates -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; psychiatric (non-organic) mental illness -> Biological Psychiatry ; clinical diagnostic and therapeutic practice guidelines, patient-management protocols, and health-system-level treatment of neurological disease -> Neurology
flagship_journals: Neurology; Annals of Neurology; Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry

scope: Study of the neurobiology of sensory systems, including vision, hearing, olfaction, taste, and touch. Covers sensory receptor physiology, neural sensory-processing pathways, and the basic science of sensory disorders.
includes: visual system neuroscience; auditory system neuroscience; olfaction and gustation; somatosensation and touch; sensory receptor physiology; sensory processing pathways in the brain
excludes: clinical diagnosis/treatment of eye disease -> Ophthalmology ; clinical diagnosis/treatment of ear, nose and throat disease -> Otorhinolaryngology
flagship_journals: Journal of Neurophysiology; Vision Research; Hearing Research

scope: Research on the ethical, legal, regulatory, and professional-accountability dimensions of nursing practice: informed consent, patient rights, confidentiality, scope-of-practice regulation, professional codes of conduct, and ethical decision-making by nurses. A currently underused subfield expected to gain topics on nursing ethics, law, and regulation.
includes: nursing ethics and moral distress; informed consent in nursing care; patient rights and advocacy; confidentiality and privacy in care delivery; professional regulation and licensure; codes of conduct and accountability; end-of-life and bioethical decision-making in nursing contexts
excludes: nursing workforce administration, staffing, and organizational leadership -> Leadership and Management ; nursing research methodology and theory development -> Research and Theory
flagship_journals: Nursing Ethics; JONA'S Healthcare Law, Ethics and Regulation

scope: Research on leadership, management, and organizational behavior within nursing and nursing-led healthcare settings: nurse staffing and workforce planning, nurse manager/executive roles, organizational culture, quality improvement leadership, and health-system administration as practiced by nursing professionals. A currently underused subfield expected to gain topics on nursing administration and workforce.
includes: nurse staffing and workforce planning; nurse manager and nurse executive roles; organizational culture and change management in nursing; quality improvement leadership; nursing workforce retention and burnout (management angle); healthcare team leadership
excludes: generic business/corporate management theory outside a nursing/healthcare setting -> Strategy and Management ; nursing ethics, legal, and regulatory issues -> Issues, ethics and legal aspects
flagship_journals: Journal of Nursing Management; Journal of Nursing Administration; Nursing Management

scope: Study of human nutrition: dietary intake, nutrient and food composition, and the health effects of diet, nutrients, and supplements. Covers clinical, public-health, and community nutrition/dietetics practice. ARBITRATION vs Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law [Environmental Science]: this card owns the health/nutritional-effect framing of diet; environmental-footprint and sustainability-impact assessment of food systems and diets belongs to Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law (2308).
includes: dietary intake and patterns; macro- and micronutrient research; food composition analysis; diet-disease relationships; dietary supplements and fortification; clinical and public-health dietetics
excludes: food processing, engineering and industrial food technology -> Food Science ; agricultural production of food crops/animals -> Agronomy and Crop Science ; environmental-footprint and sustainability-impact assessment of diets and food systems (life-cycle, land-use, greenhouse-gas framing), as opposed to the health/nutrition effects of diet -> Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law
flagship_journals: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition; British Journal of Nutrition; Nutrients

scope: Research on nursing science itself: research methodology, theory and model development, philosophy of nursing science, and evidence-based practice frameworks used to generate and evaluate nursing knowledge.
includes: nursing theory and conceptual model development; nursing research methodology; evidence-based practice frameworks; philosophy and epistemology of nursing science; instrument/scale development and validation in nursing; knowledge translation in nursing
excludes: ethical/legal governance of research and consent processes -> Issues, ethics and legal aspects ; administrative or workforce-focused nursing research -> Leadership and Management
flagship_journals: Nursing Research; Advances in Nursing Science; Research in Nursing & Health; Nursing Science Quarterly

scope: Research on the identification and early-stage design of new therapeutic drug candidates. Covers medicinal chemistry, target identification, lead-compound discovery, and structure-activity relationship studies for novel agents, including natural-product leads. ARBITRATION vs Inorganic Chemistry [Chemistry]: this card owns metal-based compounds pursued as therapeutic drug candidates (metal-drug design, SAR toward a therapeutic agent); the fundamental coordination/organometallic chemistry of metal complexes as chemistry belongs to Inorganic Chemistry (1604).
includes: medicinal chemistry; drug target identification; lead compound discovery and optimization; structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies; high-throughput and virtual screening; computer-aided/computational drug design; natural product-derived drug leads
excludes: formulation and delivery of already-identified drug substances -> Pharmaceutical Science ; mechanism of action/pharmacodynamics of established drugs -> Pharmacology ; papers whose core contribution is synthetic methodology, with bioassay/screening data present only as an add-on validation rather than the paper's focus -> Organic Chemistry ; fundamental synthesis, structure, bonding, and reactivity chemistry of metal complexes and coordination compounds studied for their own chemical properties rather than as candidate therapeutic agents -> Inorganic Chemistry
flagship_journals: Journal of Medicinal Chemistry; Drug Discovery Today; European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry

scope: Study of the formulation, delivery, and physicochemical behavior of drug products. Covers drug delivery systems, solubility and dissolution, and pharmaceutical technologies including transdermal and nanoparticle-based delivery.
includes: drug delivery systems; solubility and dissolution of drugs; transdermal and topical delivery; nanoparticle/nanomedicine drug carriers; pharmaceutical formulation and manufacturing; biopharmaceutics
excludes: identification of new drug candidates/targets -> Drug Discovery ; pharmacodynamic/pharmacokinetic mechanisms of drug action -> Pharmacology
flagship_journals: International Journal of Pharmaceutics; European Journal of Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics; Journal of Controlled Release

scope: Study of how drugs and bioactive compounds act on biological systems: pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and receptor-ligand mechanisms. Broadly includes phytochemistry and bioactivity of natural/plant-derived compounds studied for their pharmacological effects. ARBITRATION: screening extracts or compounds for bioactivity and characterising their action belongs here; isolating and optimising a defined lead goes to Drug Discovery; the practice, ethnobotany or clinical trial of a traditional remedy goes to Complementary and alternative medicine. ARBITRATION vs Pharmacology [Medicine]: basic pharmacodynamic/receptor-mechanism research and phytochemical/natural-compound bioactivity and screening stay here; clinical pharmacotherapy and drug management of patients belong to Pharmacology [Medicine].
includes: pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics; receptor and drug-target interactions; phytochemistry and bioactive natural compounds; medicinal plant pharmacology; alkaloid and natural-product pharmacology; drug interaction studies
excludes: molecular/genetic mechanisms of gene or protein function without a pharmacological framing -> Molecular Biology ; traditional/herbal medicine practice and clinical alternative therapies -> Complementary and alternative medicine ; identification of novel drug candidates/leads -> Drug Discovery ; the pharmaceutical industry and medicines as an economic, regulatory or policy object (pricing, regulation, publication bias, marketing) -> Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health ; clinical pharmacotherapy, drug management, and adverse-effect treatment as practiced on patients in a medical/clinical setting -> Pharmacology ; prescribing behaviour and medication use in clinical practice -> Pharmacology
flagship_journals: British Journal of Pharmacology; Pharmacological Reviews; Journal of Ethnopharmacology

scope: Study of the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and environmental agents on living organisms. Covers mechanisms of toxicity, forensic toxicology, ecotoxicology, and toxicological risk assessment. ARBITRATION for drug safety: post-marketing surveillance, pharmacovigilance and adverse-drug-reaction research stay here when the adverse effect itself is the object; go to Epidemiology only when the contribution is the population-level study design, and to Public Health when it is regulation or policy.
includes: mechanisms of chemical/drug toxicity; forensic toxicology and drug analysis; environmental toxicology and ecotoxicology; toxicokinetics and xenobiotic metabolism; toxicological risk assessment
excludes: therapeutic pharmacodynamics/pharmacokinetics of drugs at normal doses -> Pharmacology
flagship_journals: Toxicological Sciences; Toxicology; Archives of Toxicology

scope: Physics of sound and ultrasound, including wave propagation, acoustic materials, and ultrasonic transduction. Covers noise and vibration, underwater and architectural acoustics, and the physical principles behind ultrasonic sensing and imaging.
includes: acoustic wave propagation; ultrasonic transducers and sensors; acoustic metamaterials; noise and vibration control; underwater acoustics; architectural/room acoustics; physical principles of ultrasound imaging
excludes: clinical use of ultrasound for medical diagnosis/imaging -> Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging
flagship_journals: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America; Ultrasonics; Applied Acoustics

scope: Study of celestial objects and phenomena and the physics of the universe as a whole. Covers observational and theoretical work on stars, galaxies, planets, cosmology, and high-energy astrophysical phenomena.
includes: stellar astrophysics; galactic and extragalactic astronomy; cosmology and large-scale structure; planetary science and exoplanets; gravitational waves and pulsars; gamma-ray bursts and supernovae; astronomical instrumentation and observation
excludes: purely mathematical study of geometric/topological structures (differential geometry, the mathematics of general relativity) pursued as mathematics rather than as astrophysical modeling of real celestial systems -> Geometry and Topology ; design, development and engineering of the detectors, telescopes and instruments themselves, as opposed to the astrophysical phenomena they observe -> Instrumentation ; nuclear reaction and particle-physics theory pursued as nuclear/particle physics rather than as an astrophysical process -> Nuclear and High Energy Physics ; space policy, space law, and international/political governance of space activity -> Political Science and International Relations
flagship_journals: The Astrophysical Journal; Astronomy & Astrophysics; Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

scope: The physics of solid and liquid matter, especially collective quantum and many-body phenomena: electronic structure, superconductivity, magnetism, and phase transitions. Covers both theoretical and experimental study of ordered and disordered condensed phases, including topological and strongly correlated systems. ARBITRATION vs Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics [Physics and Astronomy]: this card owns collective/many-body condensed-phase phenomena; physics at the level of individual atoms, molecules, and photons belongs to Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics (3107).
includes: superconductivity; magnetism and spin systems; quantum many-body physics; phase transitions and critical phenomena; topological matter; strongly correlated electron systems; fundamental semiconductor physics; soft condensed matter
excludes: engineering and applications of optical/magnetic/electronic materials -> Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials ; fundamental atomic, molecular, and photon-level physics (atomic spectroscopy, cold-atom systems, quantum optics) as opposed to bulk/collective condensed-phase phenomena -> Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
flagship_journals: Physical Review B; Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter; Nature Physics; Reports on Progress in Physics

scope: The design, development, and physics of scientific instruments and measurement apparatus used in physics and astronomy research: detectors, sensors, spectrometers, telescopes, and metrology systems. Focuses on the instrument itself (its physics and engineering) rather than the phenomena it is used to study.
includes: particle and radiation detectors; sensors for physical measurement; spectrometers and analyzers; astronomical instrumentation and telescopes; metrology and calibration; measurement techniques; microscopy instrumentation
excludes: fundamental atomic, molecular, and photon-level physics phenomena studied for their own sake, even when using optical/laser techniques, rather than the instrument/apparatus itself as the contribution -> Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics ; medical/biological sensing and diagnostic device engineering designed for clinical or biological use -> Biomedical Engineering ; astrophysical phenomena and celestial observations studied as astronomy, as opposed to the design of the telescope/detector hardware itself -> Astronomy and Astrophysics ; mechanical/structural behavior of instrument materials under load, studied as a materials-mechanics question rather than instrument design -> Mechanics of Materials
flagship_journals: Review of Scientific Instruments; Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A; Measurement Science and Technology

scope: The physics of atomic nuclei, elementary particles, and fundamental forces, together with the astrophysics and cosmology that connect to particle-scale physics: nuclear structure and reactions, particle collisions, and the origin and composition of the universe including dark matter.
includes: particle physics theory and experiment; nuclear structure and reactions; high-energy collider physics; astroparticle physics; cosmology and the early universe; dark matter and dark energy; quantum field theory; string theory
excludes: radiation dosimetry, protection and applied radiation physics -> Radiation
flagship_journals: Physical Review D; Journal of High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics A; Physics Letters B

subfield_name: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
scope: The physics of atoms, molecules, and their interaction with light: structure and dynamics of atomic and molecular systems, quantum optics, laser physics, and spectroscopy. Includes cold-atom and ultracold-matter physics, atom/photon-based quantum information, and fundamental scattering and collision processes. ARBITRATION vs Condensed Matter Physics [Physics and Astronomy]: this card owns physics at the level of individual atoms, molecules, and photons (spectroscopy, cold atoms, quantum optics); collective/many-body solid-state phenomena (dielectric response, ferromagnetism, piezoelectricity, superconductivity) belong to Condensed Matter Physics (3104).
includes: quantum optics; atomic and molecular spectroscopy; laser-matter interaction; cold atoms and Bose-Einstein condensates; molecular structure and dynamics; photonics as fundamental physics; atom/photon quantum information; electron and atom scattering
excludes: semiconductor devices, optoelectronic circuits and engineering applications of optics -> Electrical and Electronic Engineering ; materials-science characterization of optical/magnetic properties of solids -> Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials ; fundamental solid-state and many-body physics of condensed phases (dielectric response, ferromagnetism, piezoelectricity, superconductivity) studied as bulk/collective phenomena rather than atomic/molecular/photon-level physics -> Condensed Matter Physics
flagship_journals: Physical Review A; Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics; Optics Express; Journal of the Optical Society of America B

scope: The physics of radiation production, propagation, interaction with matter, and detection, plus its applied dimensions: dosimetry, shielding, health physics, and radiation-based measurement and therapy technologies. Distinguished from Nuclear and High Energy Physics by its focus on radiation as a phenomenon and tool rather than on nuclear/particle structure itself. ARBITRATION vs Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging [Medicine] and Oncology [Medicine]: this card owns the physics of radiation production, propagation, interaction, dosimetry, and detection; clinical/diagnostic use of radiation and radiobiological/health effects belong to Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging (2741); clinical delivery and outcomes of radiotherapy as cancer treatment belong to Oncology (2730).
includes: ionizing and non-ionizing radiation physics; radiation dosimetry and measurement; radiation protection and health physics; radiation effects on matter; radiation sources and generation; medical radiation physics: dosimetry, treatment-planning physics, and radiation-generation technology underlying radiotherapy (as distinct from clinical delivery and outcomes)
excludes: nuclear reaction theory and particle collision physics -> Nuclear and High Energy Physics ; clinical delivery and outcomes management of radiotherapy as cancer treatment -> Oncology ; biological and cellular effects of radiation studied for clinical/health outcomes (radiobiology in a clinical-health framing), and the clinical/diagnostic use of radiation-based imaging and dose management in patient care -> Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging
flagship_journals: Radiation Physics and Chemistry; Physics in Medicine & Biology; Radiation Research; Journal of Radiological Protection

scope: Statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and the physics of nonlinear and complex systems: chaos and dynamical systems, stochastic processes, self-organization and pattern formation, plasma physics, and physics-derived models of complex/social phenomena.
includes: statistical mechanics and thermodynamics; nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory; stochastic processes; complex systems and network physics; plasma and fusion physics; self-organization and pattern formation; agent-based and sociophysics models
excludes: quantum optics, cold-atom, and photonic nonlinear dynamics studied as atomic/molecular/optical physics phenomena rather than as general statistical-mechanics or complex-systems theory -> Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics ; network science and graph-theoretic analysis of communication/computer networks as a networking-engineering discipline -> Computer Networks and Communications ; rigorous mathematical-physics formalism (functional analysis, operator theory) for foundational physical theories, pursued as mathematical physics rather than statistical/nonlinear physics modeling -> Mathematical Physics ; condensed-matter electronic/magnetic many-body phenomena in solids, studied as condensed-matter physics rather than general statistical-mechanics/complex-systems theory -> Condensed Matter Physics
flagship_journals: Physical Review E; Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science; Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications

scope: The last-resort, general/introductory bucket for psychological research that is broad, foundational, or cross-cutting enough that it does not clearly belong to one specific psychology subfield (clinical, cognitive, developmental, social, neuropsychology, applied). Use only when a topic genuinely spans or precedes specialization within psychology.
includes: general psychological theory and history of psychology; psychological methods and measurement not tied to one subfield; introductory/survey psychology topics; cross-cutting psychological science that does not fit a named subfield
excludes: applied/professional psychology practice -> Applied Psychology ; clinical psychopathology, diagnosis, and treatment -> Clinical Psychology ; cognition, perception, and experimental laboratory research -> Experimental and Cognitive Psychology ; interpersonal, group, and societal psychological processes -> Social Psychology ; child/lifespan and educational psychology -> Developmental and Educational Psychology
flagship_journals: American Psychologist; Psychological Bulletin; Perspectives on Psychological Science

scope: The application of psychological theory and methods to practical problems in real-world, non-clinical settings such as work, sport, law, consumer behaviour, and human-system design. Focuses on psychology in applied institutional or professional contexts rather than basic research on mental processes.
includes: work and organizational psychology; sport and performance psychology; forensic and legal psychology; consumer psychology; human factors and ergonomics; environmental and community psychology; occupational health psychology
excludes: basic experimental study of cognition, perception and memory -> Experimental and Cognitive Psychology ; organizational behaviour and human-resource practice studied as management -> Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management ; ergonomics and human-system interaction as design of work systems and environments -> Human Factors and Ergonomics ; interaction with computing systems where the interface or user experience is the object -> Human-Computer Interaction
flagship_journals: Journal of Applied Psychology; Applied Psychology: An International Review; Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology

scope: The assessment, understanding, and treatment of mental illness and psychological distress. Covers psychopathology, psychotherapy and treatment techniques, clinical assessment and diagnosis, and applied clinical research on conditions such as depression, anxiety, PTSD, and eating disorders.
includes: psychopathology and diagnosis; psychotherapy techniques and outcomes; clinical assessment instruments; mood, anxiety, and trauma disorders; eating disorders and behaviors; suicide and self-harm research; mental-health treatment in clinical/community settings
excludes: biological/neural mechanisms of mental disorders studied primarily at the neuroscience level -> Biological Psychiatry ; psychiatric diagnosis and pharmacological/medical treatment framed as clinical medicine -> Psychiatry and Mental health ; normative child/adolescent development and educational-context psychology not centered on clinical disorder -> Developmental and Educational Psychology
flagship_journals: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology; Clinical Psychology Review; Journal of Abnormal Psychology

scope: Psychological development across the lifespan (especially childhood and adolescence) and the psychology of learning, teaching, and educational assessment. Covers cognitive, social and emotional development and the individual-level psychological processes underlying instruction and achievement. ARBITRATION vs Education [3304]: individual-level cognitive, social and emotional developmental processes, learning mechanisms, and psychological assessment of learners stay here; education systems, curriculum, policy, and institutional teaching practice go to Education.
includes: child and adolescent development; lifespan developmental psychology; learning and instruction processes; educational and psychological assessment/testing; literacy and numeracy development; teacher-student psychological dynamics
excludes: education systems, policy, curriculum and pedagogy as an institutional field -> Education ; social influence, attitudes, and group-level processes in children, adolescents, or adults treated as social-psychological phenomena rather than developmental/learning processes -> Social Psychology
flagship_journals: Developmental Psychology; Child Development; Journal of Educational Psychology; British Journal of Educational Psychology

scope: The experimental study of mental processes using laboratory-based methods: perception, attention, memory, learning, language, reasoning, and decision-making. Covers basic cognitive science research on how the mind processes information.
includes: cognitive psychology; perception and attention; memory research; psycholinguistics; judgment and decision-making; experimental learning theory; creativity and problem-solving research
excludes: brain-behavior and physiological/biological bases of cognition -> Neuropsychology and Physiological Psychology ; applied, professional or organizational uses of psychology -> Applied Psychology
flagship_journals: Cognitive Psychology; Journal of Experimental Psychology; Cognition; Psychonomic Bulletin & Review

scope: The study of brain-behavior relationships and the physiological/biological bases of psychological processes, including clinical neuropsychology and psychophysiology. Concerned with how neural and bodily systems underlie cognition, emotion, and behavior.
includes: clinical neuropsychology; physiological psychology; psychophysiology; brain-behavior relationships; biological correlates of cognition and emotion; neuropsychological assessment of brain injury/disease
excludes: purely behavioral/experimental study of cognition without a physiological/neural focus -> Experimental and Cognitive Psychology
flagship_journals: Neuropsychologia; Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology; Biological Psychology; Psychophysiology

scope: The scientific study of how individuals' thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are shaped by social context: attitudes, group processes, interpersonal relationships, emotion, identity, and culture. Covers both individual-level social cognition and group/intergroup phenomena.
includes: attitudes and persuasion; group dynamics and intergroup relations; interpersonal relationships; emotion research; social cognition and identity; stress, coping and well-being; cross-cultural psychology; prejudice and stereotyping
excludes: social structure, institutions, and macro-level group processes analyzed as sociology rather than as an individual's psychological mechanism of social cognition or behavior -> Sociology and Political Science ; neural or brain-imaging-based mechanisms of social, emotional, or moral processing where the neuroscience method and brain-level explanation is the primary contribution -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; the developmental trajectory of social or emotional skills in children and adolescents, studied as a topic of lifespan development rather than adult social-psychological process -> Developmental and Educational Psychology ; workplace, organizational, forensic, sport, or consumer application settings where the applied/professional context is the framing rather than basic social-psychological theory -> Applied Psychology
flagship_journals: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology; Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin; European Journal of Social Psychology

scope: Last-resort bucket for social-science research that is broadly interdisciplinary, methodological, or does not map cleanly onto a single social-science subfield. Covers general social-science theory, methods, and multidisciplinary social research spanning several subfields at once.
includes: interdisciplinary social research; social science research methods; general social theory; multidisciplinary area studies; science, technology and society (general); social research on cross-cutting societal issues
excludes: research with a clear political-institutional focus -> Political Science and International Relations ; research centered on gender/sexuality as the primary lens -> Gender Studies ; research centered on legal doctrine or institutions -> Law ; interdisciplinary humanities scholarship whose object is texts, arts, ideas or the past as culture -> General Arts and Humanities
flagship_journals: Social Science Quarterly; Social Science Research; SAGE Open

scope: Archaeology practiced as a social/behavioral science: the study of past human societies through material remains, using anthropological method and theory — settlement patterns, social organization, subsistence and technology, cultural evolution, and scientific/quantitative archaeological methods (archaeometry, bioarchaeology, spatial analysis). Distinct from the identically-named Arts and Humanities subfield, which covers archaeology as a historical/humanistic and art-historical discipline (classical antiquity, epigraphy, museum and heritage scholarship framed humanistically). ARBITRATION vs Archeology [Arts and Humanities] (1204): social-scientific/anthropological-method, settlement/society-focused, and archaeometric archaeology stays here; humanistic, art-historical, classical/philological, and heritage-as-culture interpretation of antiquity goes to the Arts and Humanities twin.
includes: settlement pattern and social organization studies; archaeological method and theory; bioarchaeology and archaeometry; cultural evolution and technology in past societies; landscape and spatial archaeology; cultural resource management / heritage management (social-science framing)
excludes: humanistic, art-historical, classical, and philological study of antiquity and its material/textual heritage -> Archeology ; long-run cultural-historical narrative of colonialism, trade networks, kinship, and indigenous societies, where ethnographic/historical-anthropological synthesis is the primary contribution rather than field method, artifact analysis, or site-based archaeological science -> Anthropology
flagship_journals: Journal of Anthropological Archaeology; American Antiquity; World Archaeology

scope: Interdisciplinary social-science research on international and economic development: growth, poverty, inequality, and social change in low- and middle-income countries, and the policies, institutions, and interventions intended to promote development. ARBITRATION vs Geography, Planning and Development [3305] and Urban Studies [3322]: developing-country growth, poverty, inequality, and aid/institutional-effectiveness framing stays here regardless of spatial scale; spatial/GIS and regional-planning method goes to Geography, Planning and Development; city-scale governance and urban socio-spatial dynamics goes to Urban Studies. ARBITRATION vs General Agricultural and Biological Sciences [Agricultural and Biological Sciences]: rural development and rural sociology in developing-country contexts is named as belonging here rather than to the agricultural-science catch-all.
