includes: development studies and theory; poverty and inequality in developing countries; development policy and aid effectiveness; institutions and governance for development; developing-country economic and social change; sustainable development (social/policy angle); rural development and rural sociology in developing-country contexts
excludes: formal macroeconomic growth theory and econometric modeling of development -> Economics and Econometrics ; spatial, urban, or regional planning dimensions of development -> Geography, Planning and Development ; city-scale governance, housing, and urban socio-spatial dynamics, where the urban scale rather than the developing-country/development-studies framing is the object -> Urban Studies
flagship_journals: World Development; Journal of Development Studies; Development and Change

scope: The study of education as a system and practice: teaching and learning methods, curriculum, educational policy, institutions, and educational technology. Covers education at the classroom, institutional, and policy level, broadly and inclusively across all levels of schooling and lifelong learning. ARBITRATION vs Developmental and Educational Psychology [3204]: education systems, curriculum, pedagogy, and institutional/policy practice stay here; individual-level cognitive, social and emotional developmental processes and psychological assessment of learners go to Developmental and Educational Psychology.
includes: pedagogy and teaching methods; curriculum studies; educational policy and systems; teacher education and professional development; higher education studies; educational technology and e-learning; comparative and international education; educational leadership and administration
excludes: information systems/technology infrastructure and management as the core research object -> Information Systems ; individual-level learning psychology, child development and psychological assessment -> Developmental and Educational Psychology ; neural or brain-imaging-based investigation of learning and cognition where neural mechanism, not educational practice or policy, is the object of study -> Cognitive Neuroscience ; interpretation, criticism and theory of literary texts -> Literature and Literary Theory
flagship_journals: Educational Researcher; British Educational Research Journal; Computers & Education; Higher Education

scope: Human and regional geography, spatial analysis, and the planning and development of places at scales from local to regional to global. Covers geographic information systems and spatial methods, regional/rural development, geographic thought and pedagogy, and area/place-based studies. ARBITRATION vs Development [3303] and Urban Studies [3322]: spatial/geographic method and regional-planning practice at any scale stays here; poverty/inequality/aid-effectiveness framing of low- and middle-income-country change goes to Development; city-scale governance and urban socio-spatial dynamics goes to Urban Studies.
includes: geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial analysis; regional and rural development planning; human-environment geography; geography education and pedagogy; historical and cultural geography; area studies with a geographic/spatial framing; tourism geography
excludes: urban-specific governance, planning, and socio-spatial dynamics with a city/urban focus -> Urban Studies ; continental- or global-scale environmental/climate change analysis -> Global and Planetary Change ; poverty, inequality, and international/economic-development outcomes in low- and middle-income countries, analyzed through development theory and aid/policy effectiveness rather than spatial/geographic method -> Development ; management, marketing, and business-operations analysis of the tourism, hospitality, and travel industries, as opposed to the geographic/spatial study of place and destination -> Tourism, Leisure and Hospitality Management
flagship_journals: Journal of Geography and Regional Planning; Applied Geography; Progress in Human Geography; Regional Studies

scope: Health studied through a social-science lens: the social, political, and behavioral determinants and consequences of health and illness, health disparities and inequities, and health as it intersects with social structure (race, migration, violence, human rights). Not clinical or biomedical health research. ARBITRATION vs Public Health [Medicine]: health inequalities and social determinants analysed as social structure, policy and human rights stay here; the same determinants analysed for population health outcomes and prevention belong to Public Health.
includes: social determinants of health; health disparities and inequities; sociology/anthropology of health and illness; health and human rights; violence and health outcomes; migration and health; health-related social policy
excludes: clinical, epidemiological, or biomedical public health research -> Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
flagship_journals: Social Science & Medicine; Sociology of Health & Illness; Journal of Health and Social Behavior

scope: The behavioral and social-science study of how humans interact with systems, tools, environments, and organizations, aimed at improving usability, safety, and wellbeing: human-centered design, workplace ergonomics, cognitive and physical workload, and user-system interaction. ARBITRATION vs Human-Computer Interaction [Computer Science]: this card owns workplace, organizational and physical human-system performance (ergonomics, workload, safety) beyond the computing interface; interface design, interaction techniques and UX of computing systems belong to Human-Computer Interaction (1709).
includes: human-computer/human-system interaction; workplace and occupational ergonomics; cognitive workload and usability; human-centered/user-centered design; physical ergonomics and workstation design; error and performance in human-machine systems
excludes: engineering-side systems safety, reliability, and quality analysis -> Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality ; interaction techniques, interface design and user experience of computing systems as the object -> Human-Computer Interaction
flagship_journals: Human Factors; Applied Ergonomics; Ergonomics; International Journal of Industrial Ergonomics

scope: Legal studies covering legal theory, doctrine, and institutions across jurisdictions: constitutional, criminal, international, human-rights, and regulatory law, legal history, and jurisprudence. Includes comparative and interdisciplinary legal analysis where law itself is the object of study.
includes: legal theory and jurisprudence; constitutional and administrative law; international and comparative law; human rights law; criminal law and justice systems; environmental and regulatory law; legal history; law and language/interpretation
excludes: policy-making, governance, and institutional politics without doctrinal legal analysis -> Political Science and International Relations
flagship_journals: Harvard Law Review; Yale Law Journal; American Journal of International Law; Journal of Legal Studies; Law and Society Review

scope: Study of how information and knowledge are organized, managed, retrieved, and used by people and institutions, including library and archival practice, information behavior, and scholarly communication metrics. A social-science lens on information, distinct from the technical engineering of information systems. ARBITRATION vs Information Systems [1710]: the social-science study of information behavior, library/archival practice, and scholarly-communication metrics stays here; the technical design, engineering, and organizational management of information systems and databases goes to Information Systems.
includes: library science and administration; archival science; information retrieval and organization; information literacy and behavior; bibliometrics and scientometrics; digital libraries and knowledge management; scholarly communication
excludes: technical design/engineering of software information systems and databases -> Information Systems
flagship_journals: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology; Library & Information Science Research; Journal of Documentation; Scientometrics

scope: Language studied through a social-science lens: sociolinguistics, language policy and planning, multilingual education, language acquisition in social context, and the social functions and dynamics of language use in communities and institutions.
includes: sociolinguistics; language policy and planning; multilingual education; language and identity/society; second-language acquisition (social/educational framing); discourse and communication in social context
excludes: formal theoretical linguistics, philology, and humanities-based literary/language study -> Language and Linguistics
flagship_journals: Language in Society; Journal of Sociolinguistics; Applied Linguistics

scope: Social and behavioral science research on safety: human behavior, policy, and social systems that produce or prevent injury, accidents, and disasters — occupational safety behavior, road and traffic safety, injury prevention, disaster/risk perception, and public safety policy.
includes: occupational safety behavior and culture; road and traffic safety; injury prevention and epidemiology (behavioral/policy angle); disaster and emergency risk perception; public safety policy; workplace accident causation (human/organizational factors)
excludes: engineering systems safety, reliability, and quality analysis -> Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality ; occupational disease, hazard exposure and worker health outcomes as the object (as opposed to safety behaviour, culture and injury prevention) -> Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
flagship_journals: Journal of Safety Research; Accident Analysis & Prevention; Safety Science

scope: The broad core of sociology and political science: social structure and change, social institutions, group and intergroup dynamics, political systems and behavior, governance, social movements, crime and deviance, and migration — spanning both disciplines as ASJC groups them together. ARBITRATION vs Political Science and International Relations [3320] and Public Administration [3321]: broad/foundational sociological and social-structural framing of institutions, politics, and group behavior stays here (per ASJC's combined-subfield design); specialized political-science/IR research (comparative politics, IR theory, security studies, electoral behavior, policy analysis) goes to Political Science and International Relations; the operational management of public-sector organizations and service delivery goes to Public Administration.
includes: social theory and social structure; political systems, institutions, and behavior; social movements and collective action; crime, deviance, and criminal justice; migration and integration; intergroup relations and social conflict; public opinion and governance
excludes: individual and small-group psychological processes studied as psychology rather than sociology -> Social Psychology ; political behavior, comparative politics, international-relations theory, security/conflict studies, and policy analysis framed as specialized political-science research, rather than as one strand of a broader combined sociology-and-political-science inquiry -> Political Science and International Relations ; public-sector organizational management, bureaucracy, civil service, and public-service-delivery framed as public-management/administration practice rather than social-structural or political-behavioral analysis -> Public Administration
flagship_journals: American Sociological Review; American Journal of Sociology; American Political Science Review; British Journal of Sociology

scope: Transportation planning, policy, logistics, and mobility from a social-science and planning perspective: how people and goods move, transport systems governance, and travel behavior. Distinct from the engineering design of vehicles or transport infrastructure.
includes: transportation planning and policy; logistics and supply chain systems; public transit and urban mobility; transport economics and policy; travel behavior and human mobility analytics; traffic systems management
excludes: engineering design of roads, rail, or transport infrastructure -> Civil and Structural Engineering ; vehicle/powertrain engineering design -> Automotive Engineering
flagship_journals: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice; Journal of Transport Geography; Transport Policy; Transportation

scope: The comparative study of human societies, cultures, and their histories: ethnography, cultural and social anthropology, and the broader historical anthropology of colonialism, trade, exchange, and indigenous cultures. Overlaps naturally with archaeology where anthropology addresses long-run cultural history. ARBITRATION vs Cultural Studies [3316] and Communication [3315]: ethnographic, fieldwork-based study of specific societies' kinship, ritual, subsistence and social organization stays here; critical/theoretical analysis of culture, identity, ideology and representation goes to Cultural Studies; the study of media systems, messaging, and communication technology goes to Communication. ARBITRATION vs Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics [Agricultural and Biological Sciences]: this card owns human cultural and social evolution and the history of societies' customs/institutions; the biological evolution, phylogenetics, and behavioral ecology of organisms belongs to Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics (1105).
includes: ethnography and cultural anthropology; historical anthropology of colonial encounters, diaspora and exchange systems; indigenous cultures and history; kinship and social organization; cultural exchange and diffusion; historical and maritime anthropology
excludes: excavation-based, material-culture-focused archaeological fieldwork and method -> Archeology ; the critical/theoretical analysis of contemporary popular culture, media representation, identity politics, and ideology, where cultural theory rather than ethnographic fieldwork is the method -> Cultural Studies ; the study of media systems, journalism, and communication technology and its social effects, as opposed to ethnographic study of a society's communicative or symbolic practices -> Communication ; documentary/political history of colonial administration, trade, or indigenous polities studied as historical narrative rather than as ethnographic or anthropological-theoretical analysis -> History ; biological evolution, phylogenetics, and behavioral ecology of non-human organisms, and the biological/physical basis of human evolution, as opposed to cultural and social anthropology -> Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics
flagship_journals: American Anthropologist; Current Anthropology; Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

scope: The study of human communication processes, media, and messaging: mass and interpersonal communication, journalism, media effects, public relations, and the social role of communication technologies. Covers both theory of communication and empirical study of media systems and practices. ARBITRATION vs Cultural Studies [3316] and Anthropology [3314]: the empirical study of media, messaging, and communication processes/technology stays here; critical/theoretical analysis of culture, identity and ideology as an end in itself goes to Cultural Studies; ethnographic fieldwork on a specific society's kinship/ritual/social organization goes to Anthropology. ARBITRATION vs Human-Computer Interaction [Computer Science]: this card owns computer-mediated communication as behavior, content, and social process; the design and evaluation of interfaces and interaction techniques for communication tools belongs to Human-Computer Interaction (1709).
includes: media and mass communication studies; journalism studies; public relations and crisis communication; social media and political communication; advertising and persuasive communication; organizational and interpersonal communication; communication technology adoption
excludes: ethnographic study of culture, kinship, ritual, and social organization within a specific society, rather than the study of communication processes, media, and messaging -> Anthropology ; critical/theoretical analysis of cultural meaning, identity, ideology, and power as an end in itself, as opposed to the empirical study of media systems, messaging, and communication practice -> Cultural Studies ; information-system/technology-platform design and organizational deployment (e.g. expert-finding and retrieval infrastructure), as opposed to the substantive content and social process of communication -> Information Systems ; the design and evaluation of user interfaces and interaction techniques for computer-mediated communication tools, as opposed to the communication behavior, content and social process those tools carry -> Human-Computer Interaction
flagship_journals: Journal of Communication; Communication Research; New Media & Society; Public Relations Review

scope: The interdisciplinary study of culture, cultural practices, and cultural meaning-making: how identity, ideology, and power are produced and contested through texts, media, and everyday cultural life. Draws on critical theory to analyze popular culture, representation, and subcultures. ARBITRATION vs Anthropology [3314] and Communication [3315]: critical/theoretical analysis of cultural meaning-making, identity, ideology and power stays here; ethnographic fieldwork on a specific society's social organization goes to Anthropology; empirical study of media systems, messaging, and communication technology goes to Communication.
includes: cultural theory and criticism; identity studies (race, gender, class as cultural phenomena); popular culture analysis; media representation and textual analysis; postcolonial studies; subcultures and lifestyle studies; heritage and memory studies
excludes: ethnographic fieldwork-based study of a specific society's kinship, ritual, subsistence, or social organization, where anthropological method rather than cultural/critical theory is the primary approach -> Anthropology ; empirical study of media systems, journalism practice, and communication-technology adoption, as opposed to the critical/theoretical analysis of culture and representation -> Communication ; gender and sexuality as the primary analytical lens (feminist theory, LGBTQ+ studies, women's/men's studies) rather than a broader cultural-studies analysis of identity, ideology, and power -> Gender Studies
flagship_journals: Cultural Studies; European Journal of Cultural Studies; International Journal of Cultural Studies

scope: The study of population size, structure, and dynamics: fertility, mortality, migration, aging, and the methods used to measure and project population change, plus the social implications of demographic trends.
includes: fertility and mortality trends; population aging; migration as a demographic process; population projection and demographic methods; household and family demography; demographic transition
excludes: poverty, inequality, and development-policy analysis in low- and middle-income countries, where demographic indicators serve a development-studies argument rather than the study of population dynamics itself -> Development ; the spatial/geographic distribution and regional-planning implications of population patterns, where geographic method is the primary framing rather than demographic measurement or theory -> Geography, Planning and Development ; migration and household/family patterns analyzed as social-structural or political phenomena (integration policy, social movements) rather than as demographic measurement of population processes -> Sociology and Political Science
flagship_journals: Demography; Population and Development Review; Population Studies

scope: Research on gender and sexuality as social, cultural, and political constructs, including feminist theory, gender identity and roles, and LGBTQ+ studies across societies and historical periods. Covers how gender intersects with power, representation, language, and everyday life.
includes: feminist theory and criticism; gender identity and roles; sexuality and LGBTQ+ studies; women's and men's studies; masculinity studies; gender and language/representation; intersectionality (gender x race/class)
excludes: gender as a policy/governance variable in electoral or institutional politics -> Political Science and International Relations ; gender-based rights framed as statutory/constitutional law -> Law
flagship_journals: Gender & Society; Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society; Feminist Studies; Journal of Gender Studies; Sex Roles

scope: Studies of human development, ageing, and life transitions from a sociological/social-structural perspective: how social roles, institutions, cohorts, and biographical trajectories unfold from birth to death, and how social position at one life stage shapes outcomes at later stages. Covers life-course theory, cohort and generational analysis, transitions (school-to-work, marriage, retirement), and the social patterning of ageing.
includes: life-course theory; cohort and generational analysis; ageing and the life cycle (sociological); biographical/trajectory research; transitions to adulthood and retirement; intergenerational relations; social determinants of ageing
excludes: individual psychological development across the lifespan -> Developmental and Educational Psychology ; clinical/medical geriatrics and age-related disease -> Geriatrics and Gerontology ; population-level age structure and demographic ageing statistics -> Demography
flagship_journals: Advances in Life Course Research; Journal of Aging Studies; Ageing & Society

scope: Study of political systems, institutions, behavior, and international relations: comparative politics, public policy and governance, political theory, security and conflict studies, and foreign policy analysis. Covers both domestic politics and interstate/global political dynamics. ARBITRATION vs Sociology and Political Science [3312] and Public Administration [3321]: specialized political-science and international-relations research stays here; broad social-structural, migration, crime/deviance, and social-movement analysis (even when it touches politics) goes to Sociology and Political Science; the operational management of public agencies and bureaucracies goes to Public Administration.
includes: comparative politics; international relations theory and diplomacy; public policy and governance; political behavior and public opinion; security, conflict and peace studies; political theory and philosophy; elections and voting behavior
excludes: doctrinal analysis of statutes, constitutions, or court decisions -> Law ; gender/sexuality as the primary analytical lens even when applied to politics -> Gender Studies ; broad social-structural, social-movement, migration, crime/deviance, and intergroup-conflict analysis where sociology is the primary disciplinary lens even when the topic touches politics or governance -> Sociology and Political Science ; the operational management, administration, and organizational practice of public-sector agencies and bureaucracies, as opposed to political institutions, behavior, or policy-analysis theory -> Public Administration
flagship_journals: American Political Science Review; International Organization; Journal of Politics; World Politics; Foreign Affairs

scope: The study and practice of managing public-sector organizations, government agencies, and the delivery of public services. Covers bureaucracy and organizational behavior in the public sector, public management, public sector reform, e-government, civil service, local/regional government administration, and implementation of public programs. ARBITRATION vs Political Science and International Relations [3320] and Sociology and Political Science [3312]: the operational management, administration, and organizational practice of public-sector agencies stays here; formal policy-making and political institutions/behavior as objects of study go to Political Science and International Relations; broader social-structural/political theory of the state and power goes to Sociology and Political Science.
includes: public sector management; bureaucracy and civil service; public administration reform; e-government and digital government; local and regional government; public service delivery; nonprofit/NGO administration
excludes: formal policy-making processes, political institutions, and policy analysis -> Political Science and International Relations ; public health program administration -> Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health ; broad social and political theory of the state, power, and institutions, treated as sociological or political-science inquiry rather than public-management practice -> Sociology and Political Science
flagship_journals: Public Administration Review; Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory; Public Management Review

scope: Study of cities and urbanization: urban planning, governance, growth, and socio-spatial dynamics, including urban policy, urban culture and heritage, and the relationship between urban and rural development. Focuses on the city/region as a social and spatial unit. ARBITRATION vs Geography, Planning and Development [3305] and Development [3303]: city/urban-scale governance, housing, and socio-spatial dynamics stay here; non-urban spatial/regional-planning method goes to Geography, Planning and Development; developing-country poverty/inequality/aid-effectiveness framing goes to Development.
includes: urban planning and governance; urbanization and city growth; urban policy and housing; urban geography and sociology; city/urban network dynamics; urban heritage and culture; urban-rural development linkages
excludes: regional/rural development analysis without an urban focus -> Geography, Planning and Development ; architectural design of individual buildings -> Architecture ; IoT sensor networks and network architecture underlying smart-city technology, when the core contribution is the network/connectivity engineering -> Computer Networks and Communications ; e-government information-systems implementation (design/deployment of digital-government IT systems), when the core contribution is the information-systems work -> Information Systems ; poverty, inequality, and aid/institutional-effectiveness analysis of low- and middle-income countries, when the developing-country/development-studies framing (not the urban scale) is the object -> Development
flagship_journals: Urban Studies; Journal of Urban Affairs; Cities; International Journal of Urban and Regional Research

scope: Veterinary medicine and health care specific to horses and other equids: clinical medicine, surgery, reproduction, lameness/orthopedics, and welfare of equine species, including performance and racehorse health. SPECIES-RESTRICTED: horses only. Livestock, poultry and farmed fish go to Animal Science and Zoology; companion animals go to Small Animals.
includes: equine clinical medicine; equine surgery; equine reproduction and breeding; equine lameness and orthopedics; equine infectious and parasitic disease; equine nutrition; performance/racehorse health
excludes: general animal production/husbandry science not focused on equine clinical health -> Animal Science and Zoology ; small companion animal (dog/cat) clinical medicine -> Small Animals
flagship_journals: Equine Veterinary Journal; Journal of Equine Veterinary Science; Equine Veterinary Education

scope: Veterinary medicine and clinical care for companion/small animals, primarily dogs and cats: internal medicine, surgery, diagnostics, welfare, and behavior in small-animal clinical practice. SPECIES-RESTRICTED: companion animals only. Livestock, poultry and farmed fish go to Animal Science and Zoology.
includes: small animal internal medicine; companion animal surgery; canine and feline disease; small animal diagnostics; small animal welfare and behavior; small animal nutrition
excludes: large/production animal (livestock) medicine -> Animal Science and Zoology ; horse-specific veterinary medicine -> Equine ; laboratory-animal husbandry, welfare and model development as a research-practice question rather than veterinary clinical care -> Animal Science and Zoology
flagship_journals: Journal of Small Animal Practice; Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association; Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery; Veterinary Surgery
